dot.schmitt.function: Triggers once when a value crosses a high threshold, rearms below a low one.

dot.schmitt~.builtin_alternative: thresh~ — signal threshold with hysteresis, no averaging
dot.schmitt~.comments: Set average, low, high and gain.
dot.schmitt~.function: Detects triggers from a signal's envelope with high and low thresholds.

dot.sign.function: Outputs 1, -1 or 0 for the sign of a number.

dot.sinusoid.properties~.function: Tracks the magnitude, phase and frequency of a sine-like signal.

dot.slip.decode.comments: Common when microcontrollers send OSC over USB serial. Pair with dot.io.serial.
crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
dot.slip.decode.function: Decodes SLIP-framed bytes from a serial stream.

crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
dot.slip.encode.function: Encodes bytes into SLIP frames for serial transmission.

dot.slope.comments: Second outlet gives the absolute slope. A simple velocity estimate.
dot.slope.function: Outputs the slope between successive values using their timing.

dot.spherical.function: Converts 3D Cartesian coordinates to spherical coordinates.

dot.spherical.tocartesian.function: Converts spherical coordinates to 3D Cartesian coordinates.

dot.split.function: Routes numbers by whether they fall inside a range, allowing infinite bounds.

dot.stream.vis.builtin_alternative: multislider — can scroll data in a similar way
dot.stream.vis.comments: Use as a bpatcher for quick sensor monitoring.
dot.stream.vis.function: Displays a scrolling graph of incoming data.

dot.system.bitdepth.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
dot.system.bitdepth.function: Reports whether Max is running as 32- or 64-bit.

dot.timing.debounce.builtin_alternative: speedlim — outputs the latest message after the wait, instead of ignoring it
dot.timing.debounce.comments: Argument sets the delay in ms. Standard fix for buttons and switches that bounce.
crossref: Rhythm & time: delays, gates & bang logic
dot.timing.debounce.function: Passes a message, then ignores new ones until a delay passes.

dot.timing.metro.comments: Refpage lists wrong messages (freq/phase/bandwidth). Use arguments for low and high time, e.g. dot.timing.metro 100 1000.
dot.timing.metro.function: Bangs at random intervals within a low–high range.

dot.timing.pipe.builtin_alternative: pipe — now delays numbers, lists or symbols too
dot.timing.pipe.category: Rhythm & time: delays, gates & bang logic
dot.timing.pipe.function: Delays any message, including lists and symbols.

dot.timing.speedlim.category: Rhythm & time: delays, gates & bang logic
dot.timing.speedlim.function: Limits message rate like speedlim without its occasional freezing.

dot.timing.squeuedlim.category: Rhythm & time: delays, gates & bang logic
dot.timing.squeuedlim.function: Limits message rate but queues messages instead of dropping them.

dot.timing.thresh.builtin_alternative: thresh — now combines numbers, symbols and lists
dot.timing.thresh.category: Rhythm & time: delays, gates & bang logic
dot.timing.thresh.function: Groups messages arriving close together into one list, including symbols.

dot.timing.translate.function: Converts between Max time units like ms, ticks and note values.

dot.transfer.builtin_alternative: function — breakpoint curve you can also use for mapping
dot.transfer.comments: Arguments set table size, exponent and scale, or a saved table name. Messages edit, open, write, revert.
dot.transfer.function: Reshapes control values through a drawable transfer curve.

dot.urn.comments: Right inlet puts numbers back in the pot; seed message for repeatable results.
dot.urn.function: Outputs random numbers without repeats until all are used.

dot.vector.distance.category: Lists & data: sorting, shuffling & set operations
dot.vector.distance.comments: Argument - finds minimum distance, + finds maximum. Outputs index and distance.
dot.vector.distance.function: Finds the list item nearest to (or farthest from) a number.

dot.vector.dotproduct.builtin_alternative: vexpr — list math, needs a summing step
dot.vector.dotproduct.function: Computes the dot product of two lists.

dot.vector.interpolate.2.builtin_alternative: vexpr — can do the math by formula
dot.vector.interpolate.2.comments: Great for morphing between two parameter presets from one sensor. Values outside 0–1 extrapolate.
dot.vector.interpolate.2.function: Blends between two equal-length lists with one coefficient.

dot.vector.interpolate.4.comments: An XY pad morph between four presets.
dot.vector.interpolate.4.function: Blends four equal-length lists from an XY position.

dot.vector.normalize.function: Scales a list, or a windowed stream, into a 0–1 range.

dot.window.timed.builtin_alternative: zl.stream — keeps the last N items, by count not time
dot.window.timed.function: Collects values from the last stretch of time into a list.

modal_analysis.comments: Play notes in, then bang to analyze. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
crossref: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
modal_analysis.function: Guesses which mode a set of played notes belongs to.

modal_analysis+.comments: Extended modal_analysis wired to modal_shift and modal_mutation. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
crossref: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
modal_analysis+.function: Analyzes played notes for their mode and suggests closely related modes.

modal_change.comments: Core of the Modal Object Library: other modal_* objects read its output. It does not filter notes itself; pair with modal_coll_filter and modal_filter for that.
modal_change.function: Sets a tonic and mode and outputs that scale's pitch data.

modal_chord_analysis.comments: Beta. Gives only one of several possible functions for a chord.
crossref: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
modal_chord_analysis.function: Names a chord's root, quality, inversion and function from a note list.

modal_coll_filter.comments: Feed it from modal_change; modal_filter then reads the coll. Covers major, harmonic/melodic minor and harmonic major modes.
modal_coll_filter.function: Builds a coll that maps all 12 pitch classes onto the current mode.

modal_filter.comments: Argument names the coll filled by modal_coll_filter. Remaps notes rather than blocking them.
modal_filter.function: Snaps incoming MIDI notes to the nearest note of the current mode.

modal_fuzzharm.comments: Double-click to edit weights; feeds modal_triad. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_fuzzharm.function: Picks a chord for each scale degree using weighted probabilities.

modal_line.builtin_alternative: line (ramps through all numbers, not scale steps)
modal_line.comments: Beta; author calls it a kludge. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_line.function: Ramps between two notes using only notes of the current mode.

modal_mediant.comments: Select a tonic first. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_mediant.function: Lists modes in chromatic-mediant relation to the current one in a menu.

modal_messiaen10.comments: Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_messiaen10.function: Outputs the pitches of a 10-note Messiaen mode on a chosen tonic.

modal_messiaen6.comments: Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_messiaen6.function: Outputs the pitches of a 6-note mode, such as whole tone, on a tonic.

modal_messiaen8.comments: Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_messiaen8.function: Outputs the pitches of an 8-note mode, such as octatonic, on a tonic.

modal_messiaen9.comments: Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_messiaen9.function: Outputs the pitches of a 9-note Messiaen mode on a chosen tonic.

modal_mutation.comments: Needs modal_change in the patch to supply the current mode. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_mutation.function: Finds a mode sharing six of seven notes with the current mode and tonic.

modal_netreceive.builtin_alternative: udpreceive (general UDP; you format the data)
modal_netreceive.comments: Pair with modal_netsend. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_netreceive.function: Receives modal_change settings sent over the network.

modal_netsend.comments: Pair with modal_netreceive. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_netsend.function: Sends modal_change tonic and mode settings to another computer over UDP.

modal_pc_match.comments: Nine inlets take pitch data straight from modal_change; 35 outlets.
modal_pc_match.function: Reports which diatonic or chromatic scale degree an incoming pitch matches.

modal_pentatonic_coll_filter.comments: Pentatonic sibling of modal_coll_filter; use with modal_filter.
modal_pentatonic_coll_filter.function: Builds a coll mapping notes onto pentatonic modes.

modal_prog.comments: Drives modal_triad. @immediate 1 switches to a new list mid-progression.
modal_prog.function: Steps through a list of chord functions, one chord per bang.

modal_retune.comments: Output feeds a live.grid; the help patch, based on the Auto-tuna Max for Live device, converts it to retune~ messages.
modal_retune.function: Turns modal_change output into a note grid for setting retune~ scales.

modal_shift.comments: Needs modal_change in the patch to supply the current mode. Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_shift.function: Finds a related mode by changing one scale degree of the current mode.

modal_shiftlist.comments: Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_shiftlist.function: Lists modes one scale degree away from the current mode in a menu.

modal_strictmod.comments: Old .pat abstraction from 2007-era Max; no longer developed.
modal_strictmod.function: Outputs the transposition needed to move pitches from one tonic to another.

modal_triad.comments: Compiled external. Understands numbers, Roman numerals, letter names and alterations. Pairs with modal_prog and modal_change.
modal_triad.function: Builds chords from function names like 5, V/5 or Cdom7 in the current mode.

vj.VST_preset.category: Max for Live & DAW: plug-in & device hosting
vj.VST_preset.comments: Arguments: Mac plug-in, Windows plug-in, Mac preset, Windows preset. Connect its left outlet to vst~.
vj.VST_preset.function: Picks the Mac or Windows plug-in and preset file and sends load messages to vst~.

vj.banger.builtin_alternative: counter into gate (same idea, more wiring)
vj.banger.category: Rhythm & time: delays, gates & bang logic
vj.banger.comments: Argument sets number of outlets; right inlet sets direction.
vj.banger.function: Bangs its outlets one after another, forward, backward or back and forth.

vj.bankselect.comments: Name is misleading: it is a press-and-hold detector. Arguments: threshold, seconds.
vj.bankselect.function: Bangs when a value stays above a threshold for a set number of seconds.

vj.buffer_cropper.comments: Bang to calculate. Inlets set silence tolerance and how much silence to keep at each end.
vj.buffer_cropper.function: Trims silence from the start and end of a buffer~.

vj.countdown.function: Counts beats up or down at a tempo, with a start delay.

vj.filedate.function: Makes a filename-safe date and time string.

vj.filenamedaterecording.comments: First argument is the folder (default Desktop); others are file names.
vj.filenamedaterecording.function: Makes dated recording file paths for sfrecord~.

vj.filepath_folder.builtin_alternative: folder (lists a folder's files into a umenu)
vj.filepath_folder.function: Fills a umenu with the files in a folder next to the patch.

vj.filepather.function: Adds a folder beside the patch to the search path and lists its files.

vj.fileplayer.function: Plays sound or movie files with a small player interface.

vj.keysustainer.category: Gesture & hardware: computer keyboard, mouse & game controllers
vj.keysustainer.comments: Argument is the time window in ms.
vj.keysustainer.function: Holds a computer key down until no key has been pressed for a set time.

vj.lockstate.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
vj.lockstate.function: Reports and sets whether the patch is locked.

vj.number_separator.function: Splits a symbol of digits into separate numbers.

vj.open_folder.function: Opens a folder next to the patch in Finder or Explorer.

vj.platform_detection.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
vj.platform_detection.function: Reports whether the patch runs on a Mac or Windows computer.

vj.prefs_loader_filepath.comments: Only useful when building a standalone app; needs an app name set in the standalone object.
vj.prefs_loader_filepath.function: Loads file paths saved in a standalone app's preferences folder.

vj.prefs_loader_mappings.comments: Standalone-app helper; needs an app name set in the standalone object.
vj.prefs_loader_mappings.function: Loads mappings saved in a standalone app's preferences folder.

vj.prefs_loader_standalone.comments: Folder is ~/Library/Application Support/<app name>. Closing its help patch quits Max.
vj.prefs_loader_standalone.function: Creates a preferences folder for a standalone app.

vj.quickscale.comments: Arguments: tonic, mode name, tempo. Uses modal_change inside.
vj.quickscale.function: Plays a scale in a given key and mode at a tempo.

vj.random_filename.function: Adds a random number in front of a file name to avoid overwrites.

vj.switchtoggler.category: UI: buttons, pads, tabs & color pickers
vj.switchtoggler.function: Makes a set of toggles act like radio buttons.

vj.timetrial.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
vj.timetrial.function: Shows a nag screen and then quits after set minutes.

vj.toggler.category: UI: buttons, pads, tabs & color pickers
vj.toggler.function: Sets several toggles from one master toggle.

vj.windowresizer.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
vj.windowresizer.function: Saves the patch window size and position for next opening.

eu.verb~.comments: Attribute names are capitalized, e.g. Decay, Size, DryWet, Freeze.
eu.verb~.function: Adds stereo plate reverb that can freeze into a drone.

fftz.bthresher~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.bthresher~.comments: Like fftz.thresher~ with per-bin control via bin, alldamp, allthresh. Thresholds scale with @fftsize, so changing size changes the sound.
fftz.bthresher~.function: Freezes and decays each FFT bin separately using per-bin thresholds and damping.

fftz.burrow~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.burrow~.comments: Left inlet is the source, second the filter sound, then threshold and multiplier in dB. invert flips which parts are removed.
fftz.burrow~.function: Filters one sound using the changing spectrum of a second sound.

fftz.cavoc27~.comments: Needs no audio input. Start with very low gain. capture_spectrum seeds it from incoming sound.
fftz.cavoc27~.function: Generates evolving spectra from a 27-rule cellular automaton.

fftz.cavoc~.comments: Needs no audio input. Set rules with rule; external_trigger steps it on bang. Output gets much louder with oscbank on. Refpage digest 'Cross filtering' is wrong.
fftz.cavoc~.function: Generates evolving spectra from an 8-rule cellular automaton.

fftz.centerring~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.centerring~.comments: Sounds somewhat like flanging. randphases and zerophases reset the oscillators.
fftz.centerring~.function: Amplitude-modulates each frequency bin with its own oscillator.

fftz.codepend~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.codepend~.comments: Output can drop a lot in level; invert (spectral division) plus pad rebalance it. Not a long-IR reverb tool: use HIRT multiconvolve~ for that.
fftz.codepend~.function: Cross-convolves two live sounds by multiplying their spectra.

fftz.cross~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.cross~.comments: Classic vocoder-style cross synthesis. Output is peaky; the help file adds a compressor. autonorm matches gain but costs CPU.
fftz.cross~.function: Imposes one sound's spectrum on another, gated by a threshold.

fftz.dentist~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.dentist~.comments: toothcount sets how many bins survive; scramble picks new ones; setstate and showstate save and recall the set.
fftz.dentist~.function: Keeps only a chosen set of frequency bins and silences the rest.

fftz.disarrain~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.disarrain~.comments: Smooth version of fftz.disarray~. bang rescrambles; fadetime sets crossfade; third outlet reports the pattern.
fftz.disarrain~.function: Swaps frequency bins around, crossfading smoothly between arrangements.

fftz.disarray~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.disarray~.comments: switch_count sets how many bins move; topfreq limits the range. Changes are instant; use fftz.disarrain~ for smooth moves.
fftz.disarray~.function: Swaps a set number of frequency bins to scramble the timbre.

fftz.drown~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.drown~.comments: Not a zeroing gate: weak bins are multiplied by a factor, and a factor above 1 adds noise. Use fftz.scrape~ to limit it to a frequency range. Help patch uses `rel2peak`; refpage lists `adaptive`. Not checked in Max.
fftz.drown~.function: Scales down weak frequency bins to reduce noise, or boosts them.

fftz.enrich~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.enrich~.comments: Name the waveform with @buffername. The help says the buffer~ must be mono and 8192 samples long. Good for spectral distortion. Help patch sends `set_buffer`; refpage lists `setbuf`. Not checked in Max.
fftz.enrich~.function: Resynthesizes sound with an oscillator bank using a custom waveform.

fftz.ether~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.ether~.comments: invert takes the quieter bin instead. Compare fftz.vacancy~.
fftz.ether~.function: Builds a spectrum by taking the louder bin from two sounds.

fftz.leaker~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.leaker~.comments: Fade value 0 gives sound 1, 1 gives sound 2. upsieve, downsieve and randsieve change the bin order.
fftz.leaker~.function: Crossfades two sounds bin by bin through a sieve pattern.

fftz.loopsea~.comments: Record with acquire_sample. setloops, randspeed and randtransp shape the loops. Makes shimmering textures from short material.
fftz.loopsea~.function: Records a sound, then loops every frequency bin at its own length and speed.

fftz.mindwarp~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.mindwarp~.comments: Designed to undo the formant shift caused by pitch shifting, as in its help with fftz.pvoc~.
fftz.mindwarp~.function: Warps the spectral envelope to shift or correct formants.

fftz.morphine~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.morphine~.comments: Useful morph index is 0 to 1; transition sets the curve.
fftz.morphine~.function: Morphs between the spectra of two sounds.

fftz.multyq~.builtin_alternative: fffb~ or biquad~ with filtergraph~ (simpler signal-rate EQ)
fftz.multyq~.comments: Signal plus frequency, bandwidth and gain inlets for each band. Gain below 0 notches. FFT-based, so imprecise at low frequencies.
fftz.multyq~.function: Applies a four-band equalizer in the frequency domain.

fftz.pileup~.comments: clear empties it; persistence sets damping; mode picks behaviour.
fftz.pileup~.function: Holds each bin's sound until a louder event replaces it, for reverb-like sustain.

fftz.pvcompand~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.pvcompand~.comments: Threshold is in dB, about -60 to +60. Positive values make the sound peakier, negative values make it noisier.
fftz.pvcompand~.function: Exaggerates or flattens differences between loud and quiet frequency bins.

fftz.pvgrain~.comments: Despite the name, it is not a normal granulator. The help drives a groove~ sampler from its output.
fftz.pvgrain~.function: Tracks a sound's spectrum and outputs data for playing notes on a sampler.

fftz.pvharm~.builtin_alternative: gizmo~ (pitch shifter for use inside pfft~)
fftz.pvharm~.comments: Two transposition factors plus synth threshold. @lowfreq and @hifreq limit the band; osclimit caps CPU.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
fftz.pvharm~.function: Adds two pitch-shifted copies of the input to make harmonies.

fftz.pvoc~.comments: Works on live input, with no time-stretch. Use fftz.residency~ to freeze or scrub. @lowfreq and @highfreq set the band.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
fftz.pvoc~.function: Resynthesizes sound with a phase vocoder, transposing it and limiting its frequency band.

fftz.pvtuner~.comments: Built-in scales by message, such as eq12 and diatonic, or send a sorted list of frequencies in Hz. Works on chords and noise too.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
fftz.pvtuner~.function: Snaps the partials of any sound to a chosen scale.

fftz.pvwarpb~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.pvwarpb~.comments: Same as fftz.pvwarp~ but you can draw the warp curve. Name it with @buffername.
fftz.pvwarpb~.function: Warps a sound's frequencies using a curve stored in a buffer~.

fftz.pvwarp~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.pvwarp~.comments: autofunc makes a new random warp curve. Works well on voices.
fftz.pvwarp~.function: Warps a sound's frequencies non-linearly for inharmonic or formant effects.

fftz.reanimator~.comments: Argument sets analysis length (2000 in the help). Send analyze while the texture plays, then play the driver sound. Texture should be at least 2 seconds.
fftz.reanimator~.function: Resynthesizes a driver sound using the closest frames of a recorded texture sound.

fftz.resent~.comments: Learn fftz.residency~ first. Set per-bin speeds with bin, linespeed and randspeed.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
fftz.resent~.function: Records a spectral sample and plays each bin back at its own speed.

fftz.residency_buffer~.comments: Like fftz.residency~, but data lives in a named buffer~ (@buffername). Size it first using calcbuf. Several objects can share one buffer.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
fftz.residency_buffer~.function: Records spectral analysis into a buffer~ for replay at any speed and pitch.

fftz.residency~.builtin_alternative: stretch~ (time and pitch changes on a buffer~, offline)
fftz.residency~.comments: acquire_sample records; speed 0 freezes and allows scrubbing. @size sets memory length.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
fftz.residency~.function: Records sound spectrally, then replays it at any speed or pitch.

fftz.schmear~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.schmear~.comments: schmimp sets the smearing shape; shift pushes energy up or down. FFT size strongly changes the result.
fftz.schmear~.function: Smears energy across neighbouring frequency bins.

fftz.scrape~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.scrape~.comments: Works like fftz.drown~ between a knee and cutoff frequency and up to Nyquist. It does not learn a noise profile.
fftz.scrape~.function: Reduces weak frequency bins, but only above a chosen frequency range.

fftz.shapee~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.shapee~.comments: Shape width sets the amount. Its refpage description was copied from fftz.scrape~ and is wrong; trust the help file.
fftz.shapee~.function: Shapes the frequency movement of one sound with another sound.

fftz.swinger~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.swinger~.comments: Left inlet keeps amplitudes, right supplies phases. Try leaving the right inlet unconnected.
fftz.swinger~.function: Gives one sound the phases of another sound.

fftz.taint~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.taint~.comments: Level can drop a lot; invert (division) and pad help balance it.
fftz.taint~.function: Multiplies or divides the spectra of two sounds.

fftz.thresher~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.thresher~.comments: Two values: threshold (0 passes everything) and damping. Simpler than fftz.bthresher~.
fftz.thresher~.function: Sustains quiet frequency bins and lets them slowly decay.

fftz.vacancy~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.vacancy~.comments: Threshold in dB; rms tracks the input level; swapphase and invert change the mix. Compare fftz.ether~.
fftz.vacancy~.function: Builds a spectrum by taking the quieter bin from two sounds.

fftz.xsyn~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (build the same effect yourself; much more work)
fftz.xsyn~.comments: No controls beyond two inputs and FFT size. Use a speech sound as the filter and a rich sound as the source.
fftz.xsyn~.function: Filters one sound by the spectrum of another for cross synthesis.

flowSwing.audioWarp.comments: Type flowSwing.audioWarp. Warp markers can come from flowSwing.onsetDetect. Needs Max 9.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
flowSwing.audioWarp.function: Time-warps a sound in a buffer to unevenly spaced beat grids in real time.

flowSwing.envelop.comments: Driven by a phasor; outputs an envelope and MC gates. Type the dotted name, e.g. flowSwing.envelop, which loads as a bpatcher. Needs Max 9.
flowSwing.envelop.function: Draws envelopes and gate patterns aligned to uneven beat grids.

flowSwing.nested.comments: Type flowSwing.nested. Driven by a phasor. Needs Max 9.
flowSwing.nested.function: Sequences envelopes and gates on two nested uneven beat grids.

flowSwing.noise.comments: Type flowSwing.noise. Pairs with flowSwing.envelop gates. Needs Max 9.
flowSwing.noise.function: Plays polyphonic tone-to-noise synth voices from MC gate signals.

flowSwing.onsetDetect.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
flowSwing.onsetDetect.comments: Requires the FluCoMa package (fluid.bufonsetslice~). Type flowSwing.onsetDetect.
flowSwing.onsetDetect.function: Finds note onsets in a buffer and makes warp markers from them.

flowSwing.stepUI.comments: Companion to flowSwing.envelop or flowSwing.nested. Type flowSwing.stepUI.
flowSwing.stepUI.function: Edits per-step values for a FlowSwing sequencer with a step display.

flowSwing.subDiv.function: Divides a phasor ramp into segments of any relative lengths.

fluid.ampfeature~.comments: The curve behind fluid.ampslice~; use it when you want to threshold it yourself.
fluid.ampfeature~.function: Outputs a fast-minus-slow envelope signal that jumps at attacks.

fluid.ampgate~.builtin_alternative: thresh~ (simple threshold, no lookahead or minimum lengths)
fluid.ampgate~.comments: Needs a maxsize argument for lookahead/lookback.
fluid.ampgate~.function: Outputs a gate while audio stays above on and off thresholds.

fluid.ampslice~.comments: Tune the fast and slow ramp times, @onthreshold and @minslicelength.
fluid.ampslice~.function: Detects amplitude attacks in live audio and outputs slice triggers.

fluid.audiofilesin.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
fluid.audiofilesin.function: Collects all audio files in a folder into a list.

fluid.audiotransport~.comments: Two audio inputs; @interpolation sets the morph position. Smoother than a crossfade.
fluid.audiotransport~.function: Morphs between the spectra of two live sounds using optimal transport.

fluid.buf2list.builtin_alternative: array.frombuffer (reads into an array object; then array.tolist)
fluid.buf2list.category: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
fluid.buf2list.comments: The usual bridge from FluCoMa buffers to list processing. Set @axis for frame or channel order.
crossref: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
fluid.buf2list.function: Copies part of a buffer~ into a Max list.

fluid.bufampfeature~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
fluid.bufampfeature~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufampfeature~.function: Computes the fast-minus-slow amplitude curve of a buffer.

fluid.bufampgate~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
fluid.bufampgate~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufampgate~.function: Finds start and end points of loud regions in a buffer.

fluid.bufampslice~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
fluid.bufampslice~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufampslice~.function: Finds amplitude-based slice points across a whole buffer.

fluid.bufaudiotransport~.comments: Sources are set with @sourcea and @sourceb, not @source.
crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
fluid.bufaudiotransport~.function: Renders an in-between sound from two buffers using optimal transport.

fluid.bufchroma~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufchroma~.function: Analyzes pitch-class content of a buffer over time.

fluid.bufcompose~.comments: The glue of most FluCoMa offline patches.
fluid.bufcompose~.function: Copies, mixes and joins regions of buffers into a destination buffer.

fluid.bufflatten~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
fluid.bufflatten~.comments: Used to turn stats buffers into one data point for fluid.dataset~. It does not mix down audio.
fluid.bufflatten~.function: Lays a multichannel buffer's values out end to end in one channel.

fluid.bufhpss~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufhpss~.function: Splits a buffer into harmonic, percussive and residual parts.

fluid.bufloudness~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufloudness~.function: Analyzes loudness and true peak across a buffer.

fluid.bufmelbands~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufmelbands~.function: Analyzes mel-band energies across a buffer.

fluid.bufmfcc~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufmfcc~.function: Analyzes MFCC timbre features across a buffer.

fluid.bufnmfcross~.comments: Slow; run offline on short files.
fluid.bufnmfcross~.function: Rebuilds a target sound using pieces of a source sound's spectrum.

fluid.bufnmfseed~.function: Suggests starting bases and a component count for NMF decomposition.

fluid.bufnmf~.comments: Learned bases feed fluid.nmffilter~ and fluid.nmfmatch~ for live use.
fluid.bufnmf~.function: Decomposes a buffer into a chosen number of spectral components.

fluid.bufnoveltyfeature~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
fluid.bufnoveltyfeature~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufnoveltyfeature~.function: Computes a curve of how much a buffer's sound character changes.

fluid.bufnoveltyslice~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
fluid.bufnoveltyslice~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufnoveltyslice~.function: Finds slice points where a buffer's sound character changes.

fluid.bufonsetfeature~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
fluid.bufonsetfeature~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufonsetfeature~.function: Computes a spectral-change onset curve across a buffer.

fluid.bufonsetslice~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
fluid.bufonsetslice~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs. @metric picks one of ten change measures (0 = energy).
fluid.bufonsetslice~.function: Finds onset slice points in a buffer from spectral change.

fluid.bufpitch~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs. @algorithm: 0 cepstrum, 1 harmonic product spectrum, 2 YinFFT.
fluid.bufpitch~.function: Analyzes pitch and pitch confidence across a buffer.

fluid.bufscale~.function: Rescales a buffer's values from one range to another.

fluid.bufselectevery~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
fluid.bufselectevery~.function: Copies every Nth frame or channel of a buffer.

fluid.bufselect~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
fluid.bufselect~.function: Copies chosen frames and channels of a buffer to another buffer.

fluid.bufsinefeature~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufsinefeature~.function: Tracks sinusoidal peak frequencies and magnitudes across a buffer.

fluid.bufsines~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufsines~.function: Separates a buffer into sinusoids and a noisy residual.

fluid.bufspectralshape~.comments: Offline version of the real-time object; writes results to a buffer. Runs on bang; cancel stops long jobs.
fluid.bufspectralshape~.function: Analyzes seven spectral shape features, such as centroid and flatness, across a buffer.

fluid.bufstats~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.bufstats~.comments: Standard step from per-frame analysis to one data point per slice. @numderivs adds statistics of the rate of change.
fluid.bufstats~.function: Summarizes analysis over time as means, deviations and percentiles.

fluid.bufstft~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ (real-time spectral processing, not offline buffers)
fluid.bufstft~.function: Computes or inverts a short-time Fourier transform of a buffer.

fluid.bufthreaddemo~.comments: A tutorial object; it does no useful work.
fluid.bufthreaddemo~.function: Demonstrates FluCoMa background-thread processing, for learning only.

fluid.bufthresh~.function: Zeroes buffer values below a threshold.

fluid.buftransientslice~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers

fluid.chroma~.function: Analyzes live pitch-class content as a chroma list.

fluid.concataudiofiles.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
fluid.concataudiofiles.function: Joins a list of audio files into one buffer~.

fluid.datasetquery~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.datasetquery~.function: Filters and selects rows and columns of a FluCoMa dataset.

fluid.dataset~.builtin_alternative: coll (stores lists, no machine learning tools)

fluid.grid~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.grid~.comments: Good after fluid.umap~ for pad or grid controllers.
fluid.grid~.function: Snaps 2D dataset points onto an evenly filled grid.

fluid.hpss~.comments: @maskingmode has three options (0 soft, the default).
fluid.hpss~.function: Splits live audio into harmonic, percussive and residual parts.

fluid.jit.plotter.comments: Use instead of fluid.plotter when thousands of points make it slow.
fluid.jit.plotter.function: Plots very large 2D datasets quickly using OpenGL.

fluid.kdtree~.comments: Core of corpus lookup: fit it on a dataset, then query with knearest and a buffer.
fluid.kdtree~.function: Finds the nearest neighbours of a point in a dataset quickly.

fluid.kmeans~.comments: fitpredict writes each point's cluster to a fluid.labelset~; predictpoint labels single live points.
fluid.kmeans~.function: Groups dataset points into a chosen number of clusters.

fluid.knnregressor~.function: Predicts output values by averaging the nearest training examples.

fluid.labelset~.function: Stores text labels for dataset points, for classification.

fluid.list2buf.builtin_alternative: array.tobuffer (writes an array object to a buffer)

fluid.list2buf.comments: The usual way to turn a list into a FluCoMa data point. @autosize only resizes from the main thread.

fluid.list2buf.function: Writes a Max list into a buffer~.

fluid.loudness~.builtin_alternative: peakamp~ (raw peak level, no loudness weighting)
fluid.loudness~.function: Measures live loudness and true peak in dB.

fluid.mds~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.mds~.comments: Has only fittransform, so it cannot place new points later; fluid.umap~ and fluid.pca~ can.
fluid.mds~.function: Reduces dataset dimensions while keeping distances between points.

fluid.mfcc~.function: Analyzes live timbre as MFCC coefficients.

fluid.mlpclassifier~.comments: Slower to train than fluid.knnclassifier~ but can learn harder boundaries.
fluid.mlpclassifier~.function: Classifies data with a trainable neural network.

fluid.mlpregressor~.function: Learns a mapping from inputs to outputs with a neural network.

fluid.nmffilter~.function: Separates live audio into components using pre-learned spectral bases.

fluid.nmfmatch~.function: Reports how strongly each pre-learned spectral component is present live.

fluid.nmfmorph~.function: Cross-synthesizes a target with a source's spectral components.

fluid.normalize~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.normalize~.comments: Learn with fit on a fluid.dataset~; scale single live points with transformpoint. inversetransform undoes it.
fluid.normalize~.function: Rescales dataset columns to a set minimum and maximum.

fluid.noveltyfeature~.function: Computes a live curve of how much the sound character changes.

fluid.noveltyslice~.comments: Suits sections and textures more than individual notes.
fluid.noveltyslice~.function: Detects live changes in sound character and outputs slice triggers.

fluid.onsetfeature~.function: Computes a live spectral-change onset curve.

fluid.onsetslice~.comments: @metric picks one of ten change measures (0 = energy).
fluid.onsetslice~.function: Detects live onsets from spectral change and outputs triggers.

fluid.pca~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.pca~.comments: Fast and reversible; fluid.umap~ usually gives clearer 2D maps.
fluid.pca~.function: Reduces dataset dimensions with principal component analysis.

fluid.pitch~.builtin_alternative: fzero~ (built-in pitch tracker, no algorithm choice)
fluid.pitch~.comments: @algorithm: 0 cepstrum, 1 harmonic product spectrum, 2 YinFFT (default). Confidence helps ignore noisy frames.
fluid.pitch~.function: Tracks live pitch together with a confidence value.

fluid.plotter.comments: Outputs mouse position while clicking; pair with fluid.kdtree~ to find the nearest point. fluid.jit.plotter is faster for large sets.
fluid.plotter.function: Plots and highlights 2D dataset points in a clickable display.

fluid.robustscale~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.robustscale~.comments: Learn with fit on a fluid.dataset~; scale single live points with transformpoint. inversetransform undoes it.
fluid.robustscale~.function: Scales dataset columns by median and percentiles, resisting outliers.

fluid.sinefeature~.function: Tracks live sinusoidal peak frequencies and magnitudes.

fluid.sines~.function: Splits live audio into sinusoids and a noisy residual.

fluid.skmeans~.comments: Has fit, predict and encode messages, like fluid.kmeans~ plus encoding.
fluid.skmeans~.function: Clusters dataset points by direction using spherical k-means.

fluid.spectralshape~.comments: Covers what several single-feature objects in zsa.descriptors do.
fluid.spectralshape~.function: Analyzes seven live spectral shape features, such as centroid and flatness.

fluid.standardize~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.standardize~.comments: Learn with fit on a fluid.dataset~; scale single live points with transformpoint. inversetransform undoes it.
fluid.standardize~.function: Scales dataset columns to zero mean and unit deviation.

fluid.stats.builtin_alternative: mean (running mean of all input, no window)
fluid.stats.function: Outputs running mean and standard deviation of incoming control lists.

fluid.stftpass~.function: Passes audio through FFT and back unchanged, for testing.

fluid.transientslice~.function: Detects live transients and outputs slice triggers.

fluid.transients~.builtin_alternative: abl.dsp.transientdesign~ (boosts or cuts attacks, does not separate them)
fluid.transients~.function: Separates clicks and transients from live audio.

fluid.umap~.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
fluid.umap~.comments: Best choice for 2D corpus maps; slower to fit than fluid.pca~.
fluid.umap~.function: Reduces dataset dimensions nonlinearly, keeping similar points close together.

fluid.waveform~.builtin_alternative: waveform~ (shows and edits one buffer, no feature layers)

fl.!=~.comments: The file name fl.notequals~ also loads it.
fl.!=~.function: Outputs 1 where paired frame values differ, else 0.

fl.!~.comments: The file name fl.not~ also loads it.
fl.!~.function: Outputs 1 for zero values and 0 for non-zero values.

fl.%~.comments: The file name fl.modulo~ also loads it.
fl.%~.function: Outputs the remainder of left-frame values divided by right-frame values.

fl.&&~.comments: The file name fl.and~ also loads it.
fl.&&~.function: Outputs 1 where both input frames are non-zero, else 0.

fl.*~.comments: The file name fl.times~ also loads it.
fl.*~.function: Multiplies paired values of two frames.

fl.+~.comments: The file name fl.plus~ also loads it.
fl.+~.function: Adds paired values of two frames.

fl.-~.comments: The file name fl.minus~ also loads it.
fl.-~.function: Subtracts right-frame values from left-frame values.

fl./~.comments: The file name fl.divide~ also loads it.
fl./~.function: Divides left-frame values by right-frame values.

fl.<=~.comments: The file name fl.lessthaneq~ also loads it.
fl.<=~.function: Outputs 1 where the left value is less than or equal to the right.

fl.<~.comments: The file name fl.lessthan~ also loads it.
fl.<~.function: Outputs 1 where the left frame value is less than the right.

fl.==~.comments: The file name fl.equals~ also loads it.
fl.==~.function: Outputs 1 where paired frame values are equal, else 0.

fl.>=~.comments: The file name fl.greaterthaneq~ also loads it.
fl.>=~.function: Outputs 1 where the left value is greater than or equal to the right.

fl.>~.comments: The file name fl.greaterthan~ also loads it.
fl.>~.function: Outputs 1 where the left frame value is greater than the right.

fl.abs~.function: Outputs the absolute value of every value in a frame.

fl.accumpos~.comments: Useful for spectral rolloff. Set the target with /percentage.
fl.accumpos~.function: Finds where a frame's running sum reaches a set percentage of its total.

fl.acosh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic arccosine of every value in a frame.

fl.acos~.function: Outputs the arccosine, in radians, of every value in a frame.

fl.asinh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic arcsine of every value in a frame.

fl.asin~.function: Outputs the arcsine, in radians, of every value in a frame.

fl.atan2~.function: Outputs the two-argument arctangent of paired values from two frames.

fl.atanh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic arctangent of every value in a frame.

fl.atan~.function: Outputs the arctangent, in radians, of every value in a frame.

fl.audiotrigger~.comments: A scheduler: can start a network. Any non-zero sample triggers, so feed it clicks or a gated signal, not raw audio.
fl.audiotrigger~.function: Starts a frame whenever its audio input is non-zero.

fl.biquadcoeff~.function: Calculates biquad filter coefficients from frequency, gain and Q.

fl.biquad~.builtin_alternative: biquad~ (filters a continuous signal, not frames)
fl.biquad~.comments: Pair with fl.biquadcoeff~. /reset (on by default) clears the filter memory for each new frame.
fl.biquad~.function: Filters each frame with a biquad using given coefficients.

fl.cartopol~.comments: For spectral work the inputs are real and imaginary frames from fl.fft~.
fl.cartopol~.function: Converts x, y (and z) frames into polar or spherical coordinates.

fl.cbrt~.function: Outputs the cube root of every value in a frame.

fl.ceil~.function: Rounds every value in a frame up to the next whole number.

fl.centroid~.comments: On a magnitude spectrum this gives the spectral centroid as a bin index.
fl.centroid~.function: Calculates the centroid (center of mass) of a frame.

fl.chain~.comments: A scheduler for irregular timing, such as grain onsets computed by the network itself.
fl.chain~.function: Schedules future frames at times listed in an input frame.

fl.chop~.function: Cuts a frame into several equal-length frames.

fl.clip~.function: Limits every value in a frame to a low and high bound.

fl.combinetags~.comments: Used to gather parameter changes before sending them to an object's parameter input.
fl.combinetags~.function: Merges several tagged frames into one tagged frame.

fl.complex.*~.comments: The file name fl.complex.times~ also loads it.
fl.complex.*~.function: Multiplies two complex frame pairs value by value.

fl.complex.+~.comments: The file name fl.complex.plus~ also loads it.
fl.complex.+~.function: Adds two complex frame pairs value by value.

fl.complex.-~.comments: The file name fl.complex.minus~ also loads it.
fl.complex.-~.function: Subtracts one complex frame pair from another.

fl.complex./~.comments: The file name fl.complex.divide~ also loads it.
fl.complex./~.function: Divides two complex frame pairs value by value.

fl.complex.conj~.function: Outputs the complex conjugate of each real and imaginary pair.

fl.complex.cosh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic cosine of each complex value.

fl.complex.cos~.function: Outputs the cosine of each complex value.

fl.complex.expr~.comments: Inputs are named in1, in2 and so on, not $f1. The expression is set at creation only.
fl.complex.expr~.function: Evaluates a math expression over complex frame pairs.

fl.complex.exp~.function: Outputs e raised to each complex value.

fl.complex.log10~.function: Outputs the base-10 logarithm of each complex value.

fl.complex.log~.function: Outputs the natural logarithm of each complex value.

fl.complex.pow~.function: Raises complex values to complex powers.

fl.complex.sinh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic sine of each complex value.

fl.complex.sin~.function: Outputs the sine of each complex value.

fl.complex.sqrt~.function: Outputs the square root of each complex value.

fl.complex.tanh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic tangent of each complex value.

fl.complex.tan~.function: Outputs the tangent of each complex value.

fl.constant~.function: Outputs a single constant such as pi or e, optionally scaled.

fl.contextcontrol~.comments: Messages: multithread, timeout, export. Multithreading is off by default. Point it at a network with @id. It processes no frames itself.
fl.contextcontrol~.function: Turns multithreading on or off and exports networks to C++ for a context.

fl.convert~.comments: Pick the conversion with /mode, for example amp->db.
fl.convert~.function: Converts frame values between units such as dB, MIDI and frequency.

fl.convolve~.comments: Frame-based, so it suits short kernels and spectral smoothing, not long reverb IRs.
fl.convolve~.function: Convolves two real or complex frames.

fl.copysign~.function: Gives left-frame magnitudes the signs of the right frame.

fl.correlate~.comments: Can find the lag between two frames.
fl.correlate~.function: Cross-correlates two real or complex frames.

fl.cosh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic cosine of every value in a frame.

fl.cos~.function: Outputs the cosine of every value in a frame.

fl.crest~.function: Calculates the crest factor (peak over RMS) of a frame.

fl.diff~.function: Outputs the absolute difference between paired values of two frames.

fl.dispatch~.comments: Routing is changed through parameters (/input_01 and so on).
fl.dispatch~.function: Sends each of several inputs to any of several outputs.

fl.erfc~.function: Outputs the complementary error function of every value in a frame.

fl.erf~.function: Outputs the error function of every value in a frame.

fl.exp2~.function: Outputs 2 raised to every value in a frame.

fl.expr~.comments: Inputs are named in1, in2 and so on, not $f1. One fl.expr~ replaces long chains of FrameLib math objects. Expression is fixed at creation.
fl.expr~.function: Evaluates a math expression across input frames.

fl.exp~.function: Outputs e raised to every value in a frame.

fl.fft~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ with fftin~ (fixed hop and window, signal-rate)
fl.fft~.comments: Size follows the input frame, zero-padded to a power of two; there is no size parameter. Window first with fl.window~. Get magnitude and phase with fl.cartopol~.
fl.fft~.function: Converts a frame into its spectrum as real and imaginary frames.

fl.filtertags~.function: Passes on only the tagged items whose tags match a list.

fl.firphase~.function: Changes the phase of FIR filter coefficients without changing their amplitude response.

fl.flatness~.comments: On a magnitude spectrum this is spectral flatness: near 1 for noise, near 0 for tones.
fl.flatness~.function: Calculates the flatness (noisiness) of a frame.

fl.floor~.function: Rounds every value in a frame down.

fl.fold~.function: Folds frame values back into a low and high range.

fl.framedelta~.builtin_alternative: framedelta~ (inside pfft~, phase deviation between FFT frames)
fl.framedelta~.comments: Frames must stay the same length or it resets.
fl.framedelta~.function: Outputs the change in each value since the previous frame.

fl.framemax~.function: Outputs the largest value in a frame.

fl.framemin~.function: Outputs the smallest value in a frame.

fl.frommax~.comments: One of the main entry points from Max. /mode params builds tagged frames that set other objects' parameters. Output happens only when a frame reaches its trigger input.
fl.frommax~.function: Turns Max messages into frames, or into tagged parameter frames.

fl.gaussian~.function: Generates frames of normally distributed random values.

fl.geomean~.function: Calculates the geometric mean of a frame.

fl.hypot~.comments: Gives spectral magnitude from real and imaginary frames.
fl.hypot~.function: Outputs the hypotenuse length for paired values of two frames.

fl.ifft~.builtin_alternative: pfft~ with fftout~ (fixed hop and window, signal-rate)
fl.ifft~.comments: Overlap-add the results with fl.sink~ to get audio.
fl.ifft~.function: Turns real and imaginary spectrum frames back into a time-domain frame.

fl.info~.function: Reports the sample rate, channel count and length of a buffer~.

fl.interval~.comments: The usual first object of a FrameLib network; nothing runs without a scheduler. Set the period as an argument or /interval, with /units. Set the context with @id.
fl.interval~.function: Starts a new frame at a regular interval.

fl.join~.function: Joins several frames end to end into one frame.

fl.kernelsmooth~.function: Smooths a frame using a supplied smoothing shape.

fl.kurtosis~.function: Calculates the kurtosis (peakiness) of a frame.

fl.lag~.function: Delays uniform-length frames by a whole number of frames.

fl.length~.function: Outputs the number of values in a frame.

fl.log10~.function: Outputs the base-10 logarithm of every value in a frame.

fl.log2~.function: Outputs the base-2 logarithm of every value in a frame.

fl.log~.function: Outputs the natural logarithm of every value in a frame.

fl.lookupstring~.function: Picks one stored text string by index for tagging.

fl.lookup~.comments: Only the first input triggers output. Good for waveshaping and mapping curves.
fl.lookup~.function: Reads values from a table frame at positions given by another frame.

fl.makestring~.function: Builds a tagged string from text and numbers.

fl.makewindow~.comments: Use fl.window~ instead when you just want to multiply an input by a window.
fl.makewindow~.function: Generates a window shape such as Hann as a frame.

fl.map~.function: Scales frame values from one range to another, with curves.

fl.maxpos~.comments: On a magnitude spectrum this finds the loudest bin.
fl.maxpos~.function: Outputs the index of the largest value in a frame.

fl.max~.function: Outputs the larger of each pair of values from two frames.

fl.mean~.function: Calculates the average of a frame.

fl.medianfilter~.comments: Handy for removing spikes or separating tonal and noisy spectral parts.
fl.medianfilter~.function: Replaces each value with the median of its neighbours.

fl.minpos~.function: Outputs the index of the smallest value in a frame.

fl.min~.function: Outputs the smaller of each pair of values from two frames.

fl.movingaverage~.comments: Frames must stay the same length. Separate rise and fall rates (/alpha_up, /alpha_down).
fl.movingaverage~.function: Tracks a smoothed average and deviation for each value across frames.

fl.multitaper~.function: Calculates a low-variance power spectrum using multiple tapers.

fl.nanfilter~.function: Replaces or removes invalid (NaN) values in a frame.

fl.nonzero~.function: Outputs the positions of non-zero values in a frame.

fl.once~.comments: A scheduler. Good for building a constant table once, such as a window.
fl.once~.function: Starts a single frame at the beginning of time.

fl.onepolezero~.function: Filters each frame with a one-pole, one-zero filter.

fl.onepole~.function: Filters each frame with a gentle 6 dB per octave filter.

fl.pack~.comments: Multistream is FrameLib's version of MC. A first argument like =4 also sets stream count.
fl.pack~.function: Combines several frame streams into one multistream connection.

fl.pad~.function: Adds a repeated value to the start or end of a frame.

fl.pattern~.comments: Like a step sequencer inside a network. Loop, once, pause and stop modes.
fl.pattern~.function: Steps through a frame of values one value per trigger.

fl.peaks~.comments: On a magnitude spectrum this finds partials, the basis of sinusoidal tracking.
fl.peaks~.function: Finds and interpolates peaks in a frame.

fl.perblock~.comments: A scheduler. Timing depends on the audio vector size.
fl.perblock~.function: Starts one frame at the start of each audio block.

fl.percentile~.function: Outputs a chosen percentile of a frame, the median by default.

fl.poltocar~.comments: Use before fl.ifft~ when you edited magnitudes and phases.
fl.poltocar~.function: Converts polar or spherical frames into x, y (and z) frames.

fl.pow~.function: Raises left-frame values to the power of right-frame values.

fl.prioritise~.function: Passes only the highest-priority frame when several arrive at once.

fl.product~.function: Multiplies all values in a frame together.

fl.ramp~.comments: Often used as the position frame for fl.read~ in granular patches.
fl.ramp~.function: Generates a straight-line ramp across a frame.

fl.random~.function: Generates frames of random values between 0 and 1.

fl.read~.comments: The core of FrameLib granular patches: position frame in, grain out. Choose interpolation with /interp and units with /units.
fl.read~.function: Reads values from a buffer~ at positions given by a frame.

fl.recall~.comments: Names are local to a context.
fl.recall~.function: Reads a frame stored under a name by fl.store~.

fl.register~.function: Stores a frame and outputs it again when triggered.

fl.reverse~.function: Reverses the order of values in a frame.

fl.rms~.function: Calculates the RMS level of a frame.

fl.round~.function: Rounds every value in a frame to the nearest whole number.

fl.route~.function: Sends a frame to one of several outputs.

fl.samplerate~.function: Outputs the sample rate or converts values based on it.

fl.select~.function: Passes one of several input frames to the output.

fl.shift~.function: Shifts values left or right within a frame.

fl.sinh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic sine of every value in a frame.

fl.sink~.builtin_alternative: fftout~ (audio out of a pfft~ patch)
fl.sink~.comments: The main exit from FrameLib to MSP audio. No added latency; /buffer_size limits frame length. Use this, not fl.tomax~, to hear a network.
fl.sink~.function: Turns frames back into audio by overlap-adding them.

fl.sin~.function: Outputs the sine of every value in a frame.

fl.skewness~.function: Calculates the skewness (lopsidedness) of a frame.

fl.sort~.function: Sorts a frame in ascending or descending order.

fl.source~.comments: The main entry from MSP audio. Adds latency equal to the captured length; set it with /length.

fl.spatial~.comments: Uses DBAP. Output gains must be multiplied with audio frames inside the network.
fl.spatial~.function: Computes speaker gains for a 3D position using distance-based panning.

fl.split~.function: Splits a frame into two at a given point.

fl.spread~.function: Calculates the spread of a frame around its centroid.

fl.sqrt~.function: Outputs the square root of every value in a frame.

fl.stddev~.function: Calculates the standard deviation of a frame.

fl.store~.comments: Names are local to a context, so the same name in two contexts is two stores.
fl.store~.function: Stores a frame under a name for fl.recall~.

fl.streamid~.comments: Numbers count from one. Use to give each stream different settings.
fl.streamid~.function: Outputs which stream number each stream of a multistream is.

fl.subframe~.function: Outputs a chosen section of a frame.

fl.sum~.function: Adds up all values in a frame.

fl.svf~.comments: /multi_output gives every filter mode at once.
fl.svf~.function: Filters each frame with a state-variable filter.

fl.tag~.comments: The frame-rate way to change parameters. Read tagged frames back with fl.untag~ or fl.filtertags~.
fl.tag~.function: Attaches parameter names to frames so they can set other objects.

fl.tanh~.function: Outputs the hyperbolic tangent of every value in a frame.

fl.tan~.function: Outputs the tangent of every value in a frame.

fl.ticks~.function: Counts incoming frames up or down to a limit.

fl.timedelta~.function: Outputs the time between consecutive frames.

fl.timemean~.comments: Frames must stay the same length.
fl.timemean~.function: Averages each value over the most recent frames.

fl.timemedian~.comments: Frames must stay the same length.
fl.timemedian~.function: Takes the median (or other percentile) of each value over recent frames.

fl.timer~.function: Outputs time elapsed since the last reset frame.

fl.timestddev~.function: Calculates each value's standard deviation over recent frames.

fl.tomax~.comments: The exit for data, not audio: use fl.sink~ or fl.trace~ for signals. Long frames may be cut by Max's message size limit.

fl.trace~.builtin_alternative: sig~ (holds a number as a signal)
fl.trace~.comments: For control signals, not audio: /mode picks which frame value is output.
fl.trace~.function: Outputs frame values as an audio-rate control signal held until the next frame.

fl.trunc~.function: Drops the fractional part of every value in a frame.

fl.uniform~.function: Generates frames where every value is the same.

fl.unpack~.function: Splits a multistream connection into single streams.

fl.untag~.function: Pulls named values out of a tagged frame.

fl.window~.comments: Standard step before fl.fft~. Set the shape as an argument (fl.window~ hann) or /window; /compensate adjusts gain for overlap-add.
fl.window~.function: Multiplies each frame by a window shape such as Hann.

fl.wrap~.function: Wraps frame values around a low and high range.

fl.||~.comments: The file name fl.or~ also loads it.
fl.||~.function: Outputs 1 where either input frame value is non-zero.

bufconvolve~.comments: Messages convolve and deconvolve; deconvolution tuned by deconvmode, deconvfilter, deconvrange and related attributes. Output may overwrite an input buffer safely.
bufconvolve~.function: Convolves or deconvolves two buffers offline into a third buffer.

bufresample~.builtin_alternative: stretch~ (can change pitch without changing length)
bufresample~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
bufresample~.comments: High-quality sinc resampling. Messages resample, transpose, both, filter. Transposing this way changes length, like a tape speed change.
bufresample~.function: Resamples a buffer~ to change its sample rate or transpose it.

bufreverse~.comments: Triggered by process. Bangs when done.
bufreverse~.function: Writes a reversed copy of a buffer~ to another buffer~.

hirt.convolutionreverb~.comments: Opens its own window with open; IRs load from menus or by dropping files. Damping and shape controls are applied offline, not live. Early and late parts can use different IRs.
hirt.convolutionreverb~.function: Adds a ready-made stereo convolution reverb with IR library, EQ and damping.

hirt.convolver~.comments: Use for cabinets, rooms or custom IRs when you don't need the reverb extras. Drop an IR file on its window.
hirt.convolver~.function: Convolves stereo audio with any impulse response, with EQ and width.

hirt.irmaker~.comments: Outlets 0 and 1 go to the speakers or device; 2 and 3 to your monitors. sweep for rooms and analog gear, impulse for digital systems.
hirt.irmaker~.function: Measures, auditions and saves impulse responses of rooms or devices.

iralign~.comments: Messages align (in place) and alignto (to a new buffer). Do this before averaging.
iralign~.function: Lines up several impulse responses in time.

iraverage~.comments: average works in the time domain; process works in the frequency domain, with smoothing options.
iraverage~.function: Averages several impulse responses in the time or frequency domain.

irextract~.comments: Use when the recording was made elsewhere. Settings must match those used to make the measurement signal.
irextract~.function: Turns recorded measurement signals into impulse responses.

irinvert~.comments: For room or speaker correction. mimo inverts multi-speaker systems. Regularisation via the deconv attributes avoids harsh results.
irinvert~.function: Builds an inverse filter that undoes an impulse response.

irmeasure~.comments: Supports sweeps, MLS and coloured noise, many inputs and outputs. Lower level than hirt.irmaker~. Retrieve results with getir.
irmeasure~.function: Plays test signals and records a system to measure its impulse responses.

irnonlin~.comments: For modelling mildly distorting devices. Research-level.
irnonlin~.function: Converts harmonic IRs from a sweep into a Hammerstein nonlinear model.

irphase~.comments: Messages minphase, linphase, maxphase, mixedphase, allpass. Minimum phase removes pre-ringing.
irphase~.function: Changes an impulse response's phase while keeping its frequency response.

irplapprox~.comments: Output suits iruser~ or deconvolution filter settings.
irplapprox~.function: Summarises an IR's frequency response as a short list of frequency and dB points.

irreference~.comments: Works with any excitation, even music, when a test sweep isn't possible.
irreference~.function: Estimates an impulse response by comparing a reference recording with a system recording.

irstats~.comments: Send stats with the buffer name and the measures wanted, such as t30, edt, clarity; results come out in that order.
irstats~.function: Calculates room measurements such as reverb time and clarity from an IR.

irsweeps~.comments: For measuring with another app or device. Deconvolve the recording with bufconvolve~ or irextract~.
irsweeps~.function: Writes measurement signals such as sine sweeps into a buffer~.

irtransaural~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
irtransaural~.comments: lattice needs four convolutions, shuffler two. Needs measured same-side and cross-side IRs.
irtransaural~.function: Creates crosstalk-cancellation filters to play binaural audio over two speakers.

irtrimnorm~.comments: Each operation has in-place and to-new-buffer versions, such as trim and trimto.
irtrimnorm~.function: Trims, crops, pads and normalises one or many impulse responses.

iruser~.builtin_alternative: buffir~ (plays an FIR from a buffer~ but does not design it)
iruser~.comments: Send make. Set the response and phase with attributes. Turns an EQ curve into an IR for convolution.
iruser~.function: Creates an impulse response from a frequency response you specify.

irvalue~.comments: Send set with the buffer, then a frequency in Hz.
irvalue~.function: Reports an impulse response's level in dB at a given frequency.

morphfilter~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
morphfilter~.comments: Build the chain with addfilter, run with process, reset with clear. Bangs when done.
morphfilter~.function: Applies shelf and peak filters to a buffer~ with gain changing over time.

multiconvolve~.comments: Arguments: inputs, outputs, latency mode zero, short (128 samples) or medium (512). Longer latency saves CPU. Load IRs with set. mc.multiconvolve~ also exists.
multiconvolve~.function: Convolves one or more live signals with impulse responses in realtime.

spectrumdraw~.comments: Many display attributes. set shows a buffer~'s spectrum; freeze holds live input. Mouse data comes out the outlet.
spectrumdraw~.function: Draws live or buffer~ spectra, up to four curves at once.

ddg.v2arp.comments: Attributes set direction, order, octaves and transpose. You supply the clock, for example link.beat or metro.
ddg.v2arp.function: Arpeggiates held MIDI notes, one step per bang.

ddg.v2gate.comments: Sends no note-offs; follow it with makenote.
ddg.v2gate.function: Chops a held chord into five voices played by an on/off list.

ddg.v2mono.function: Makes MIDI input behave like a monosynth keyboard, with note priority and legato.

link.audio.receive~.comments: Only between separate apps, never inside one Max. Use getchannels to list streams, then set the channel attribute. Needs the Link package, Max 9 or later. All link objects in Max share one Link peer.
link.audio.receive~.function: Receives stereo audio from another app on the Link session.

link.audio.send~.comments: Both inlets need signals. Sends with the same name are summed into one stream. Not for routing inside Max; use send~ there. Needs the Link package, Max 9 or later. All link objects in Max share one Link peer.
link.audio.send~.function: Sends stereo audio to other apps on the Link session.

link.beat.comments: lock 1 follows the shared start and stop. Setting tempo changes it for everyone. Needs the Link package, Max 9 or later. All link objects in Max share one Link peer.
link.beat.function: Bangs on beats, bars and subdivisions locked to the shared Link tempo.

link.phasor~.comments: quantum sets the number of beats in a bar. Drives signal sequencers like rtt.* objects. Needs the Link package, Max 9 or later. All link objects in Max share one Link peer.
link.phasor~.function: Outputs a ramp signal locked to the shared Link beat and phase.

link.session.comments: enable 0 leaves the session. Needs the Link package, Max 9 or later. All link objects in Max share one Link peer.
link.session.function: Starts, stops and sets tempo for a Link session, and reports changes.

nw.cppan~.function: Pans a mono signal across two outputs with constant power.

nw.gateplus~.category: Audio I/O: gain, mixers & channel strips
nw.gateplus~.function: Switches a signal on or off only at zero crossings, avoiding clicks.

nw.grainbang~.comments: Timing follows the scheduler; use nw.grainpulse~ for sample accuracy. Needs two buffer~ names as arguments: one for the sound, one for the grain window shape.
nw.grainbang~.function: Plays one grain from a buffer each time it gets a bang.

nw.grainphase~.comments: With nw.phasorshift~, builds overlapping grains for time-stretch and pitch-shift. Needs two buffer~ names as arguments: one for the sound, one for the grain window shape.
nw.grainphase~.function: Plays grains from a buffer driven by a phasor signal.

nw.grainpulse~.comments: Sample-accurate; drive with train~. Needs two buffer~ names as arguments: one for the sound, one for the grain window shape.
nw.grainpulse~.function: Plays one grain from a buffer on each pulse in a signal.

nw.grainstream~.comments: Needs two buffer~ names as arguments: one for the sound, one for the grain window shape.
nw.grainstream~.function: Plays a continuous stream of grains from a buffer at a set frequency.

nw.gverb~.comments: Mix the dry signal back in yourself.
nw.gverb~.function: Adds stereo Griesinger-style reverb; outputs only the wet signal.

nw.phasorshift~.function: Outputs several phasor signals evenly spaced in phase.

nw.pulsesamp~.comments: Sample-accurate triggering; parameter changes wait for the next segment.
nw.pulsesamp~.function: Plays a buffer segment each time a pulse signal arrives.

nw.recordplus~.comments: Loop and append are always on.
nw.recordplus~.function: Records into a buffer, starting and stopping only at zero crossings.

nw.trainshift~.function: Outputs several pulse trains evenly spaced in phase.

db.geneural.comments: Teaching demo from Dillon Bastan (2018). Training runs in classic js, prediction in gen. Hidden units max 15. FluCoMa or ml.star packages are sturdier.
db.geneural.function: Trains a tiny neural network that maps input lists to output lists.

db.mc.channelhandling.builtin_alternative: mc.voiceallocator~ — does the allocation; this only adds a lookup table for the studies.
db.mc.channelhandling.comments: Internal helper of the studies' gui.main panels. Works only with db.mc.channelmap using the same busy map name.
db.mc.channelhandling.function: Allocates MC voices and publishes a voice-to-channel lookup table.

db.mc.channelmap.category: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
db.mc.channelmap.comments: Internal helper. Listens on a global name built from the busy map name, so two patches using the same name share one table.
db.mc.channelmap.function: Reorders a list to match channels allocated by db.mc.channelhandling.

db.mc.clicklessdelay~.builtin_alternative: mc.tapin~ / mc.tapout~ — clicks when the delay time jumps.
db.mc.clicklessdelay~.comments: Arguments: busy map name, crossfade Hz. New times take effect within one crossfade cycle. Max delay 5000 ms.
db.mc.clicklessdelay~.function: Crossfades two MC delay lines so delay-time jumps never click.

db.mc.filterdelaystereo~.comments: Needs ltomc, which exists only inside study folders, not next to this file. Parameters arrive as named lists (filterCenters, delayTimes, pans...).
db.mc.filterdelaystereo~.function: Band-passes, delays and pans many copies of a sound into stereo.

db.mc.fmwavetable~.comments: Needs buffers to read, usually from db.wavetable2polybuffer. Wave messages must be prefixed carrier or modulator.
db.mc.fmwavetable~.function: Runs per-channel FM synthesis with wavetable carrier and modulator.

db.mc.geneural~.comments: Demo-grade. Its mc.gen~ codeboxes show a reusable MC-to-buffer bridge using mc_channel.
db.mc.geneural~.function: Runs the geneural neural network on MC signals, one value per channel.

db.mc.oneshotphasor~.builtin_alternative: mc.voiceallocator~ with mc.line~ — the same three objects wired by hand.
db.mc.oneshotphasor~.comments: Frees the channel automatically when the ramp reaches 1. Arguments: channel count, busy map name.
db.mc.oneshotphasor~.function: Starts a one-shot 0–1 ramp on a free MC channel per message.

db.mc.oneshotramp~.comments: Allocator is typed with the busy map name as a second argument, not @name; the refpage documents only one argument, so the name is likely ignored. Unverified in Max.
db.mc.oneshotramp~.function: Plays an attack/decay envelope on a newly allocated MC channel.

db.mc.periodiconeshot~.builtin_alternative: live.step — a full step sequencer UI, without the MC ramps.
db.mc.periodiconeshot~.comments: Messages: active, rate, steps, length, activeSteps. Depends on db.mc.oneshotphasor~.
db.mc.periodiconeshot~.function: Steps through a 0/1 pattern, firing MC one-shot ramps on active steps.

db.mc.stereodelay~.comments: Internal ltomc boxes are fixed at 32 channels regardless of the argument. Needs ltomc from a study folder.
db.mc.stereodelay~.function: Feeds a stereo signal through many randomly panned MC feedback delays.

db.mc.vox~.comments: Argument sets the band count. Band frequencies, Q and gain are set with fffb~ messages (freq, QAll, gain); the study sends them at load.
db.mc.vox~.function: Vocodes a carrier with a modulator using two MC filter banks.

db.wavetable2polybuffer.comments: Frame size must match the file (256 for the included morph.256.rom.aif). Frames are named <name>.1, <name>.2...
db.wavetable2polybuffer.function: Splits a wavetable file into one buffer per frame in a polybuffer~.

dp_osc.builtin_alternative: mc.cycle~ — the helper is three objects.
dp_osc.comments: Internal helper of the dynamicpoly study.
dp_osc.function: Turns a 0–1 MC signal into sine tones panned to stereo.

gui.main.comments: Four different patchers share this name in one package. Which one Max loads by name is not documented. Not reusable.
gui.main.function: Shows one study's control panel with presets and voice allocation.

ltomc.builtin_alternative: mc.list~ — list to MC signal, no glide; or mc.sig~ with applyvalues.
ltomc.comments: Three copies inside study folders; shared abstractions call it by name. Arguments: channels, busy map name, glide ms.
ltomc.function: Converts a number list into a smoothed MC signal, one value per channel.

mctomatrix.builtin_alternative: jit.catch~ — captures signals as matrices, one plane per signal rather than one cell per channel.
mctomatrix.comments: Arguments: channels, matrix name, plane, row. Idea by Timo Hoogland.
mctomatrix.function: Writes each MC channel's value into one cell of a jit.matrix.

MIAP.comments: Message version of MIAP~: outputs a list of node gains, useful for mapping many parameters. Real object names are capitalized: MIAP, MIAP~, MIAP.map, MIAP.meyer. Maps are saved as JSON.
MIAP.function: Interpolates values across a map of nodes you place, for panning or control.

MIAP.map.comments: Linked by name to MIAP or MIAP~. Real object names are capitalized: MIAP, MIAP~, MIAP.map, MIAP.meyer. Maps are saved as JSON.
MIAP.map.function: Draws and edits MIAP node maps and moves the listening point.

MIAP.meyer.comments: Real object names are capitalized: MIAP, MIAP~, MIAP.map, MIAP.meyer. Maps are saved as JSON.
MIAP.meyer.function: Converts Meyer Sound D-Mitri projects into MIAP map and trajectory files.

MIAP~.comments: Supports MC. Two maps (A, B) can be crossfaded; trajectories can be recorded and played. Real object names are capitalized: MIAP, MIAP~, MIAP.map, MIAP.meyer. Maps are saved as JSON.
MIAP~.function: Pans audio across any speaker layout using a map of nodes.

byte-cast.comments: Arguments set one output type per outlet. For data from Arduino serial or max-ble.
crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
byte-cast.function: Decodes lists of raw bytes into ints, floats or symbols.

max-ble.comments: Messages: scan, found, connect, device. Outputs raw bytes; decode with byte-cast. No built-in Max object reads BLE.
max-ble.function: Scans for, connects to and reads Bluetooth Low Energy devices.

FungibleData.comments: A tutorial patch opened from the help browser, not an object you can create. Uses Util.* helper abstractions from Peter Elsea's Lobjects that ship inside this folder.
FungibleData.function: Shows ways to copy data between table, coll, list, multislider and matrix.

PattrSave.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
PattrSave.comments: A demo patch, not a reusable object. By Charles Veasey.
PattrSave.function: Shows saving presets to a JSON file that reloads when the patch opens.

average.comments: Demo patch, not an object; its name only looks like one. Several boxes need third-party externals (St.Average, laverage, f0.average_tempo) that are not installed.
average.function: Compares several ways of averaging numbers, lists and tap tempo.

coll_duplicates.comments: Abstraction. Numbers only. Writes to colls named master, buf and end, so two copies interfere.
coll_duplicates.function: Removes duplicate numbers from a coll and renumbers it.

deltachange.comments: Abstraction; argument sets the change threshold.
deltachange.function: Sends values to one outlet for small changes and another for big ones.

fxwdmxusbpro.comments: Abstraction by Olivier Pasquet and fxw. Up to 512 channels, values 0-255. Pick the serial port from its menu.
fxwdmxusbpro.function: Sends DMX channel values to an Enttec DMX USB Pro interface.

imi.apploader.comments: Abstraction; needs the shell external (here an Intel-only binary in Samplor). Hard-coded paths assume Max 7's shared Packages folder, so it likely fails in Max 9.
imi.apploader.function: Opens an application stored in the package's apps folder.

imi.apploader2.comments: Abstraction. Hard-coded paths point to Max 7's shared Packages folder, so it likely fails in Max 9.
imi.apploader2.function: Opens an application in the package's apps folder via launchbrowser.

imi.avgmap.comments: Abstraction for galvanic skin sensors. Needs dot.smooth, which is not installed, and uses global value names avg, plus and minus.
imi.avgmap.function: Waits for a sensor's average, then maps nearby values to 0-10.

imi.bounce.comments: Abstraction; needs lrem from the RTC-lib package.
imi.bounce.function: Folds a moving number back and forth between 0 and a limit.

imi.counter.comments: Abstraction. Arguments: start, iterations, step, speed in ms.
imi.counter.function: Counts through a range at a set speed, or instantly with fast.

imi.debug.function: Prints a message with a time stamp to the Max console.

imi.desktop.comments: Abstraction; argument is the message to prepend, such as read or open.
imi.desktop.function: Adds the Desktop folder path in front of a file name.

imi.docloader.comments: Abstraction; needs the shell external, which here is an Intel-only binary in the Samplor package.
imi.docloader.function: Opens a document from the Max search path in its default application.

imi.draw.comments: Abstraction for jit.lcd drawing messages such as paintrect and paintoval.
imi.draw.function: Converts x, y, width, height into jit.lcd rectangle coordinates, from center or corner.

imi.encoder.comments: Abstraction; argument sets the frame count. Resets to the last frame after 5 seconds idle. Uses a global value named a.
imi.encoder.function: Turns rotary encoder pulses into movie frame numbers.
