vs_frame_delay.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Up to 70 frames; v1.7 added reverse playback.
vs_frame_delay.function: Delays video by a number of frames, with mix, feedback and random playback.

vs_hsl_modulator.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Includes a pedestal offset.
vs_hsl_modulator.function: Adjusts hue, saturation and lightness, each with a texture modulation input.

vs_hue_rot.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_hue_rot.function: Rotates the hue of a texture by hand or by another texture.

vs_huemod_2.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Same as vs_hue_rot plus saturation.
vs_huemod_2.function: Rotates hue and sets saturation, with texture hue modulation.

vs_inverter.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. With a modulation texture connected, the knob becomes an attenuverter.
vs_inverter.function: Inverts a texture's colors by hand or by a modulating texture.

vs_lfo.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Six waveforms; freq_range switches slow and fast ranges.
vs_lfo.function: Generates an LFO waveform as both a texture and a control number.

vs_luma_key.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_luma_key.function: Keys one texture over another by brightness.

vs_mixer_3.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_mixer_3.function: Adds up to three textures with level controls.

vs_mixer_3_avg.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Needs all three inputs connected to work.

vs_mixer_6.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_mixer_6.function: Adds up to six textures with level controls.

vs_mixer_fdbk.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Outputs both the pre-feedback and feedback mixes.
vs_mixer_fdbk.function: Adds three textures and boosts brightness with internal feedback.

vs_mixer_spat.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Movement follows the sync timer.
vs_mixer_spat.function: Splits the screen into four areas, each showing a different texture.

vs_mixer_spat2.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Added in v1.7.
vs_mixer_spat2.function: Replaces up to four sections of a texture with other textures.

vs_modules.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
vs_modules.comments: A menu patch, not a processing module. Vsynth's supported way to add modules is Paste From > Vsynth/menu/vs_menu.maxpat.
vs_modules.function: Shows the menu of Vsynth texture modules for adding them to a patch.

vs_noise_2.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. x and y set noise resolution; speed sets refresh rate.
vs_noise_2.function: Generates resizable white noise with optional interpolation.

vs_noise_3.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_noise_3.function: Generates animated, resizable pseudo-random noise on the GPU.

vs_noise_s.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.

vs_offset.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Useful as a constant for mixers and operators.
vs_offset.function: Generates a flat gray texture at a set brightness, plus the value as data.

vs_offset+rot.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Several edge-wrapping modes; no modulation inputs (see vs_displacement).
vs_offset+rot.function: Moves, rotates and zooms a texture.

vs_op1.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. op picks the operation; applies to all RGB planes.
vs_op1.function: Applies a math operation between a texture and a number.

vs_op2.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_op2.function: Applies a math operation between two textures.

vs_output.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Usually one per patch; several stack as layers. Drag corners for projection mapping.
vs_output.function: Shows a texture in the output window as a corner-pinnable layer.

vs_pixelator.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. dim sets horizontal resolution, up to 1280.
vs_pixelator.function: Pixelates a texture by lowering its resolution.

vs_pixelator_2.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_pixelator_2.function: Pixelates a texture with separate horizontal and vertical resolution.

vs_pixelator_nonSquare.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Added in v1.7.
vs_pixelator_nonSquare.function: Pixelates a texture into non-square shapes, four modes.

vs_poltocar.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Pairs with vs_cartopol.
vs_poltocar.function: Remaps a texture from polar to Cartesian coordinates.

vs_preview.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Passes the texture through, so it can sit in the middle of a chain.
vs_preview.function: Shows a texture in a resizable preview inside the patch.

vs_preview_floating.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. The window name can be changed and is saved with the patch.
vs_preview_floating.function: Shows a texture in a separate floating window.

vs_quad_crossfader.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_quad_crossfader.function: Crossfades between four textures with an X/Y pad.

vs_render.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Exactly one across all open patches; a duplicate causes heavy frame drops and an extra window. Sets fps, window size and texture dim.
vs_render.function: Creates the render context and output window that runs all Vsynth texture modules.

vs_rgb2luma.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_rgb2luma.function: Converts a color texture to grayscale.

vs_rgb2sepia.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_rgb2sepia.function: Tints a texture with a sepia tone.

vs_rgb2yuv.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Try with vs_hue_rot for new color schemes.
vs_rgb2yuv.function: Converts RGB color to luma and two chroma channels for color effects.

vs_rgb_mixer.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Pairs with vs_rgb_swiz for per-channel processing.
vs_rgb_mixer.function: Combines three textures as the red, green and blue channels.

vs_rgb_offstr.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Knobs act as offsets, or attenuverters when a texture is connected.
vs_rgb_offstr.function: Moves each RGB channel separately, with texture modulation inputs.

vs_rgb_swiz.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Pairs with vs_rgb_mixer.
vs_rgb_swiz.function: Splits a texture into separate red, green and blue textures.

vs_s&h.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. bang captures a new frame.
vs_s&h.function: Freezes a frame of video when triggered (sample and hold).

vs_s&h_spat.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_s&h_spat.function: Freezes parts of a frame by area, sample and hold in space.

vs_scope.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Handy for seeing waveform generator output.
vs_scope.function: Graphs the brightness levels across a texture, like a waveform display.

vs_snapshot.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. bang saves; auto mode saves every second; dpi sets resolution.
vs_snapshot.function: Saves still images of a texture to the Desktop.

vs_snapshot_2.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Variant of vs_snapshot.
vs_snapshot_2.function: Saves still images with a chosen file name and folder.

vs_sources_main.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. For trying things out; source picks the input. Not saved by the Vsynth preset system.
vs_sources_main.function: Offers several test sources (camera, movie, noise, color, oscillator) in one module.

vs_spout_client.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Windows only; requires the Spout package (jit.gl.spoutreceiver), not installed here.
vs_spout_client.function: Receives textures from other Windows apps over Spout.

vs_spout_server.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Windows only; requires the Spout package (jit.gl.spoutsender), not installed here.
vs_spout_server.function: Shares a Vsynth texture with other Windows apps over Spout.

vs_sync.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Outputs control messages, not textures. Also used to build floating-point control waveforms.
vs_sync.function: Sends the global sync timer to waveform generators and other Vsynth modules.

vs_sync_time.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Outputs control messages, not textures.
vs_sync_time.function: Sets the speed and direction of the Vsynth global timer and outputs its count.

vs_syphon_client.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Mac only; requires the Syphon package (jit.gl.syphonclient).
vs_syphon_client.function: Receives textures from other Mac apps over Syphon.

vs_syphon_server.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Mac only; requires the Syphon package (jit.gl.syphonserver). Server name is saved with the patch.
vs_syphon_server.function: Shares a Vsynth texture with other Mac apps over Syphon.

vs_title_generator.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Three typing modes; font and size are settable.
vs_title_generator.function: Renders static, scrolling or auto-typed text as a texture.

vs_transfer_curves.builtin_alternative: vz.mappr (Vizzie function mapping of R, G, B)
vs_transfer_curves.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Feed it a ramp to see the curve. Added in v1.7.
vs_transfer_curves.function: Remaps pixel brightness through one of 22 transfer curves.

vs_vca.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Formula: in1 * ((in2 * am) + bias).
vs_vca.function: Modulates one texture's brightness by another (video VCA).

vs_video_monitors.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. High-resolution mode costs more CPU.
vs_video_monitors.function: Shows waveform monitor, vectorscope, histogram or parade views of video.

vs_wavefolder.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render.
vs_wavefolder.function: Folds texture brightness with a full-wave rectifier for doubled patterns.

vs_wfg_2.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. The workhorse oscillator; normal and inverted outputs. Follows the sync timer.
vs_wfg_2.function: Generates scrolling line patterns with frequency, phase and pulse-width modulation.

vs_wfg_3.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. angle rotates the pattern; pow toggle changes the curve (v1.7).
vs_wfg_3.function: Generates scrolling lines that morph smoothly between waveforms, with modulation.

vs_wfg_av.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Not synced to the render timer.
vs_wfg_av.function: Generates a low-resolution video oscillator that also outputs audio, with FM.

vs_wfg_bipolar.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Like vs_wfg_3 but in the -1 to 1 range.
vs_wfg_bipolar.function: Generates waveform patterns centered on the screen, for symmetrical images.

vs_wfg_polarizer.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Mix of vs_wfg_bipolar and vs_wfg_rad.
vs_wfg_polarizer.function: Morphs between straight stripe and polar waveform patterns.

vs_wfg_rad.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. freq_lock snaps frequency to multiples of 60 for clean spirals.
vs_wfg_rad.function: Generates radial and spiral patterns from standard waveforms.

vs_wfg_s.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. The basic oscillator; vs_wfg_2 adds frequency modulation.
vs_wfg_s.function: Generates simple vertical scrolling line patterns with phase and pulse-width modulation.

vs_wfg_shapes.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. vertex sets polygon sides.
vs_wfg_shapes.function: Generates circles, polygons and other shapes from standard waveforms.

vs_wfg_tri_core.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Added in v1.7.
vs_wfg_tri_core.function: Generates triangle-to-ramp patterns with adjustable peak and curve.

vs_xyz_disp.comments: Vsynth texture module (a bpatcher added from the Vsynth menu); needs one vs_render. Seven draw modes; position and rotation save with presets. Try it directly in the render window.
vs_xyz_disp.function: Wraps a texture onto a 3D mesh and displaces it by brightness.

vsc_angle_encoder.comments: Vsynth control helper (bpatcher); outputs numbers to a module's control inlet.
vsc_angle_encoder.function: Endless knob for setting angle or hue on Vsynth modules.

vsc_center_ctrl.comments: Vsynth control helper (bpatcher); double-click resets. Used with vs_wfg_rad and vs_wfg_shapes.
vsc_center_ctrl.function: X/Y pad for setting the center point of Vsynth modules.

vsc_color_picker.category: UI: buttons, pads, tabs & color pickers
vsc_color_picker.function: Color picker that sends colors to Vsynth modules.

vsc_data_scope.comments: Vsynth control helper (bpatcher); data passes through.
vsc_data_scope.function: Plots control numbers over time, like a small data oscilloscope.

vsc_freq_encoder.function: Endless knob for setting frequency on Vsynth waveform generators.

vsc_presets.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
vsc_presets.comments: Paste From > Vsynth/vs_presets.maxpat. Shift-click stores; write and read save a .json file. Excludes vs_render, vs_sources_main and vector_sosci. Can morph between presets.
vsc_presets.function: Stores, recalls and morphs Vsynth module settings as presets.

vsc_spacebang.category: UI: buttons, pads, tabs & color pickers
crossref: Gesture & hardware: computer keyboard, mouse & game controllers
vsc_spacebang.function: Sends bangs and 0/1 changes when the spacebar is pressed and released.

xray.diagonalize.comments: A js script (js xray.diagonalize.js), mainly a helper for xray.jit.svd output. It sits in XRAY's jsextensions folder; Max for the Visual Arts ships a different file with the same name.
xray.diagonalize.function: Turns a row-vector matrix into a square diagonal matrix.

xray.dynamicexpr.builtin_alternative: jit.expr (set its expr attribute with a message built by sprintf)
xray.dynamicexpr.comments: A js script (js xray.dynamicexpr.js); send its output to jit.expr. Max for the Visual Arts ships a different file with the same name.
xray.dynamicexpr.function: Rewrites a jit.expr expression, filling in $1, $2 values from incoming lists.

xray.jit.3dbuffer.builtin_alternative: jit.matrixset (stores a set of matrices for resequencing)
xray.jit.3dbuffer.comments: Arguments: planes, type, width, height, frame count, buffer name. Give each instance a unique name. Pairs with xray.jit.timecube for slit-scan style effects. CPU matrices, so keep sizes small.
xray.jit.3dbuffer.function: Stores recent video frames in a 3D matrix as a circular time buffer.

xray.jit.cellcoords.comments: On means 255 for char, 1 for long or float. Handy after thresholding a camera image. out_mode picks long or float32 output.
xray.jit.cellcoords.function: Lists the coordinates of every 'on' cell in a 2D matrix.

xray.jit.cellminmax.comments: Takes 1-plane 2D matrices. mode 0 scans horizontally, 1 vertically. Useful for finding silhouette edges.
xray.jit.cellminmax.function: Finds the first non-zero cell from each side of each row or column.

xray.jit.cellvalue.comments: Support object for xray.jit.contourmap. Left inlet: any 2D matrix; right inlet: 2-plane float32 coordinates.
xray.jit.cellvalue.function: Reads matrix values at a list of cell coordinates.

xray.jit.colormap.comments: Feed the result to jit.charmap to recolor a grayscale image with another image's colors. mode 0 averages colors per brightness bin; mode 1 keeps the first.
xray.jit.colormap.function: Builds a 256-entry color map from a color image, sorted by brightness.

xray.jit.contourmap.comments: Input is a 3-plane float32 surface; draw the result with jit.gl.mesh @draw_mode lines. levels sets evenly spaced contours; mode 1 uses the isolevel list instead.
xray.jit.contourmap.function: Calculates contour lines (isolines) of a 3D height surface.

xray.jit.crossproduct.builtin_alternative: jit.gen (the help file itself says a jit.gen patch can replace it)
xray.jit.crossproduct.comments: Takes float32 or float64. normalize takes two values, 0 or 1.
xray.jit.crossproduct.function: Computes the cross product of two 3-plane vector matrices.

xray.jit.cumsum.comments: float32 or float64 matrices only. dimmode picks the dimension.
xray.jit.cumsum.function: Adds up matrix values cumulatively along one dimension.

xray.jit.distance.comments: Takes 1-plane char or long matrices. Uses city-block distance. mode sets horizontal, vertical or both passes. Good for glow, outline and distance-based effects.
xray.jit.distance.function: Computes a distance transform: how far each pixel is from the nearest shape.

xray.jit.grid2tri.comments: Use when you need to control how grid points join into triangles. Draw with jit.gl.mesh @draw_mode triangles. Accepts 2- or 3-plane matrices.
xray.jit.grid2tri.function: Converts a grid of vertices into explicit triangles for jit.gl.mesh.

xray.jit.invertrepos.comments: Most repos maps are not one-to-one, so the inverse loses detail.
xray.jit.invertrepos.function: Inverts an absolute jit.repos map so the warp can be undone.

xray.jit.keepcell.comments: Second inlet takes a matrix of cell coordinates, for example from xray.jit.cellcoords.
xray.jit.keepcell.function: Keeps only the cells listed in a second coordinate matrix and blanks the rest.

xray.jit.kmeans.comments: Takes a 1-plane matrix of vectors; clusters sets k and dimmode sets row or column vectors. You must choose k in advance.
xray.jit.kmeans.function: Groups a matrix of vectors into k clusters with the k-means algorithm.

xray.jit.line2quad.comments: mode 0 works in 2D and is faster; mode 1 handles lines with depth. scale sets quad size; normalize makes all quads the same size.
xray.jit.line2quad.function: Turns line segments into quads so lines can be drawn with width.

xray.jit.mean.builtin_alternative: jit.3m (mean of the whole matrix per plane)
xray.jit.mean.comments: Output is float32, or float64 for float64 input. meandim picks rows or columns; mean 0 gives sums instead.
xray.jit.mean.function: Outputs the mean or sum of each row or column of a 2D matrix.

xray.jit.pinv.comments: Needs the three outputs of xray.jit.svd as inputs; it does not run the SVD itself.
xray.jit.pinv.function: Computes the pseudo-inverse of a matrix from its singular value decomposition.

xray.jit.quicksort.comments: Any type, dimension and planecount. planemode picks the plane to sort by; summode sorts by the sum of planes. iterations and recursions can stop it early for glitchy partial sorts.
xray.jit.quicksort.function: Sorts matrix cells along rows or columns with the quicksort algorithm.

xray.jit.sift.comments: siftdim picks rows or columns; siftplane picks which plane of the marker matrix to read.
xray.jit.sift.function: Keeps only the rows or columns marked 'on' in a second matrix.

xray.jit.svd.comments: Outputs U, sigma (as a vector) and V, largest value first. Use xray.diagonalize to rebuild sigma as a matrix and xray.jit.pinv for the pseudo-inverse.
xray.jit.svd.function: Computes the singular value decomposition of a 1-plane matrix.

xray.jit.timecube.comments: Feed it the named buffer from xray.jit.3dbuffer. mode 0 and 1 take vertical or horizontal slices; mode 2 uses a grayscale map (right inlet) to pick a frame per pixel.
xray.jit.timecube.function: Reads a 3D frame buffer through time, slit-scan style, or by a map.

xray.jit.water.comments: Needs feedback: use the same named jit.matrix at input and output. Grids below about 100x100 are unstable. Second inlet sets wave speed per cell. Poke cells with setcell to make ripples.
xray.jit.water.function: Simulates ripples on a water surface in a float matrix.

xy.attractors~.comments: Seven attractors, e.g. gen~ @gen xyz.lorenz. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.attractors~.function: Generates moving x, y, z coordinates from strange attractors like Lorenz.

xy.fm~.comments: Load as gen~ @gen xy.fm. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.fm~.function: Generates 2D coordinates using FM synthesis math.

xy.galaxy~.comments: Load as mc.gen~ @gen xy.galaxy. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.galaxy~.function: Spreads many voices on rotating rings for multichannel panning.

xy.grains~.comments: Load as mc.gen~ @gen xy.grain. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.grains~.function: Generates random short bursts of 2D position, one per voice.

xy.manual~.comments: Load as mc.gen~ @gen xy.manual. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.manual~.function: Places each channel at a 2D position you set by hand.

xy.mass~.comments: Load as gen~ @gen xy.mass. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.mass~.function: Generates 2D motion from mass, gravity and wind physics.

xy.multi~.comments: Load as mc.gen~ @gen xy.multi. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.multi~.function: Spreads voices around a rotating circle for multichannel panning.

xy.random~.comments: Load as gen~ @gen xy.random. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.random~.function: Generates random 2D positions with smooth gliding between them.

xy.sequencer~.comments: Load as gen~ @gen xy.sequencer4 or xy.sequencer8. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.sequencer~.function: Steps through a set of 2D positions, one per step.

xy.wave~.comments: Load as gen~ @gen xy.wave. Not an object you can type: it names a help file. Use the gen~ code with gen~ @gen <name> or the package clipping.
xy.wave~.function: Generates 2D motion by combining waveforms on x and y.

abc.2plf.ui.function: Draws two breakpoint lines and plays them out as line-ready lists.

abc.adcinput~.builtin_alternative: ezadc~ — built-in input with on/off; add live.gain~ for level.
abc.adcinput~.category: Audio I/O: hardware inputs, outputs & audio settings
abc.adcinput~.function: Brings in one audio input channel with gain and optional DC filtering.

abc.audiotester~.category: Audio I/O: hardware inputs, outputs & audio settings
abc.audiotester~.comments: Worth adding to any multichannel patch before a rehearsal.
abc.audiotester~.function: Steps pink noise around each loudspeaker to test a multichannel setup.

abc.cartopol~.builtin_alternative: cartopol~ — same math on two separate signal cords.
abc.cartopol~.comments: Useful mainly because its output channel order matches what abc.hoa.map~ expects.
abc.cartopol~.function: Converts a cartesian signal pair to polar coordinates in one mc cord.

abc.delaychain~.comments: There is no abc.delaychain~ 1; an argument of 1 becomes 2. Pair with abc.mc.chopan~ to hear the stages spread in stereo.
abc.delaychain~.function: Chains up to 16 tempo-synced delays in series, one output per stage.

abc.drops~.function: Synthesises rain-drop sounds from filtered impulses.

abc.dtd.ui.comments: Only meaningful with abc.hoa.decorrelation~ in man mode.
abc.dtd.ui.function: Draws per-harmonic delay and gain curves for ambisonic decorrelation.

abc.env.noise~.function: Generates Hann-enveloped noise grains with random dropouts.

abc.envfollower~.function: Tracks a signal's amplitude envelope with separate attack and release.

abc.gaincontrol.builtin_alternative: live.gain~ — built-in dB slider that processes audio directly.
abc.gaincontrol.category: Audio I/O: gain, mixers & channel strips
abc.gaincontrol.function: Sends gain messages in dB from a slider to abclib objects.

abc.generatorinterface~.function: Provides a GUI panel for the abc.generator~ test source.

abc.generator~.function: Generates pulsed sine, sawtooth and noise test signals.

abc.gotoevent.comments: Only useful if the patch's cue system advances by counting events from its outlet.
abc.gotoevent.function: Fast-forwards through a piece's cue events to resume from a chosen one.

abc.hoa.binaural~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
abc.hoa.binaural~.comments: 2D orders 1-7, 3D orders 1-3 only. Built directly with Faust rather than RNBO, so its raw external has one extra outlet that the wrapper drops.
abc.hoa.binaural~.function: Renders an ambisonic stream binaurally for headphones.

abc.hoa.decoder~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
abc.hoa.decoder~.comments: Uses ACN channel order and N2D/SN3D normalisation (per its refpage). 3D stops at order 3. Speaker angles for irregular layouts must be sent as a<i>/e<i> messages, typically from a loadbang-fired semicolon message box.
abc.hoa.decoder~.function: Decodes an ambisonic stream to a ring or sphere of up to 16 speakers.

abc.hoa.decorrelation~.comments: man mode is 2D only. 3D exists up to order 5, beyond the other 3D objects. Large delay values allocate big buffers.
abc.hoa.decorrelation~.function: Diffuses an ambisonic field by delaying its components by different amounts.

abc.hoa.delay~.comments: 2D only. The refpage also lists a 'man' mode, but no external for it exists, so @mode man fails to build.
abc.hoa.delay~.function: Applies different delays to each ambisonic component for spatial echoes.

abc.hoa.encoder~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
abc.hoa.encoder~.comments: Order 1-7 in 2D, 1-3 in 3D. Output channel count grows with order, so decoders must use the same order. Distance is not modelled; use abc.hoa.map~ for that.
abc.hoa.encoder~.function: Encodes up to eight mono sources into a 2D or 3D ambisonic stream.

abc.hoa.grain~.function: Granulates each ambisonic component to scatter sound across the field.

abc.hoa.map~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
abc.hoa.map~.comments: Inlet count follows @sources, not the refpage. 2D only. Build the position pair with the abc objects: the refpage's stated channel order disagrees with abc.pict2map's internals.
abc.hoa.map~.function: Encodes moving sources with angle and distance into a 2D ambisonic stream.

abc.hoa.mirror~.comments: 2D only. The refpage's attribute text and its description disagree on what 0 and -1 mean; the overview patch comment matches the description.
abc.hoa.mirror~.function: Mirrors a 2D ambisonic field between left and right.

abc.hoa.optim~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
abc.hoa.optim~.comments: In 3D, orders 1-3 only. Choose the type by where the audience sits, per the refpage: maxRe for a centred audience, inPhase for one spread around the circle.
abc.hoa.optim~.function: Optimises an ambisonic stream for centred or spread-out audiences.

abc.hoa.ringmod~.function: Ring-modulates ambisonic components to create spatial modulation effects.

abc.hoa.rotate~.comments: 2D only. Rotates everything at once; to move one source use a<i>/s<i> on abc.hoa.encoder~.
abc.hoa.rotate~.function: Rotates an entire 2D ambisonic sound field by angle or speed.

abc.hoa.scope~.comments: Needs abc.scope or abc.scopeembedded to draw anything; those use Jitter OpenGL. 2D only.
abc.hoa.scope~.function: Converts a 2D ambisonic stream into signals for a circular scope display.

abc.hoa.stereodecoder~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
abc.hoa.stereodecoder~.comments: 2D only, orders 1-7. No 3D version exists; asking for @dimensions 3 builds a missing object.
abc.hoa.stereodecoder~.function: Decodes a 2D ambisonic stream to a stereo pair.

abc.hoa.stereoencoder~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
abc.hoa.stereoencoder~.comments: 2D only. Its refpage file declares the wrong object name (abc.hoa.stereodecoder~), so tools that index refpages by that name can mix the two up.
abc.hoa.stereoencoder~.function: Encodes a stereo signal as two ambisonic sources with a set opening angle.

abc.hoa.wider~.function: Widens the apparent size of sources in an ambisonic field.

abc.jupiterbank~.comments: Choose the mode with @mode 2, not a bare 2: a numeric argument is ignored by this wrapper.
abc.jupiterbank~.function: Synthesises 14 harmonic or inharmonic partials, crossfading into resonant filters.

abc.linedrive~.builtin_alternative: linedrive — same exponential mapping for messages, not signals.
abc.linedrive~.function: Maps a 0-127 signal exponentially onto a chosen output range.

abc.map.ui.comments: Click-drag moves a circle, cmd-drag changes opacity, option-drag changes radius.
abc.map.ui.function: Controls several source positions with draggable circles on a 2D map.

abc.mc.addsynth~.builtin_alternative: oscbank~ — oscillator bank driven by frequency and magnitude signals.
abc.mc.addsynth~.function: Synthesises up to 16 beating partials, one per output channel.

abc.mc.busmult~.builtin_alternative: mc.*~ — multiplies two mc signals the same way.
abc.mc.busmult~.category: Audio I/O: gain, mixers & channel strips
abc.mc.busmult~.function: Multiplies two multichannel buses channel by channel.

abc.mc.busplus~.builtin_alternative: mc.+~ — adds two mc signals the same way.
abc.mc.busplus~.category: Audio I/O: gain, mixers & channel strips
abc.mc.busplus~.function: Adds two multichannel buses channel by channel.

abc.mc.busselect~.builtin_alternative: selector~ — its ramptime attribute also crossfades, one input at a time.
abc.mc.busselect~.comments: Three inlets. Its refpage file declares the wrong object name (abc.mc.busplus~).
abc.mc.busselect~.function: Crossfades between two multichannel buses over a set time.

abc.mc.chopan~.builtin_alternative: mc.mixdown~ — mixes and pans an mc signal to fewer channels, more flexible layouts.
abc.mc.chopan~.comments: The package's standard way to hear a multichannel synth in stereo.
abc.mc.chopan~.function: Spreads up to 16 channels across stereo with constant-energy panning.

abc.mc.delay~.builtin_alternative: tapin~ — with tapout~ gives free-running delays, timed in ms.
abc.mc.delay~.function: Runs up to 16 parallel tempo-synced delay lines with feedback.

abc.mc.flanger~.builtin_alternative: abl.dsp.flanger~ — Ableton flanger, one instance per stream.
abc.mc.flanger~.function: Flanges up to 16 channels with adjustable spatial spread.

abc.mc.freqshift~.builtin_alternative: freqshift~ — built-in; mc.freqshift~ runs it per channel.
abc.mc.freqshift~.function: Frequency-shifts up to 16 channels by different amounts.

abc.mc.gain~.builtin_alternative: mc.gain~ — built-in multichannel gain slider; mc.live.gain~ adds metering.
abc.mc.gain~.category: Audio I/O: gain, mixers & channel strips
abc.mc.gain~.comments: Mostly useful inside abclib help-style patches where abc.gaincontrol already sends gain messages.
abc.mc.gain~.function: Applies one gain in dB to up to 16 channels.

abc.mc.grain~.function: Granulates up to 16 live channels with separate settings.

abc.mc.harmo~.builtin_alternative: pitchshift~ — built-in pitch shifter; mc.pitchshift~ runs it per channel.
abc.mc.harmo~.category: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
abc.mc.harmo~.function: Transposes up to 16 channels by different intervals.

abc.mc.matrix~.builtin_alternative: mcs.matrix~ — built-in routing matrix with mc input and output and a ramp attribute.
abc.mc.matrix~.function: Routes and mixes up to 16 channels with ramped gain coefficients.

abc.mc.multinoise~.builtin_alternative: mc.noise~ — with @chans n, one noise~ per channel.
abc.mc.multinoise~.function: Generates up to 16 decorrelated white-noise channels.

abc.mc.pulsedenv2synth~.function: Generates decorrelated pulsed sine bursts on up to 16 channels.

abc.mc.randenv~.function: Applies randomly muted periodic envelopes to up to 16 channels.

abc.mc.substractsynth~.builtin_alternative: fffb~ — fast fixed filter bank with separate outputs.
abc.mc.substractsynth~.function: Filters up to 16 noise channels into tuned partials.

abc.mult2pi~.function: Multiplies a signal by two pi.

abc.musdur.builtin_alternative: translate — converts Max time values, including note values, to milliseconds.
abc.musdur.function: Selects a musical note value to set abclib delay durations.

abc.peakamp~.builtin_alternative: peakamp~ — same measurement reported as messages, not a signal.
abc.peakamp~.function: Outputs a signal's peak amplitude over a moving time window.

abc.phasor2pi~.function: Generates a ramp from zero to two pi at a set frequency.

abc.pict2map.function: Positions one ambisonic source by dragging on a 2D pad.

abc.poltocar~.builtin_alternative: poltocar~ — same math on two separate signal cords.
abc.poltocar~.function: Converts a polar signal pair to cartesian coordinates in one mc cord.

abc.puckettespaf~.comments: Send a gain message: the refpage lists its current value as -127 dB. The overview patch writes 'abc.puckettespaf~ 2', which this wrapper ignores; only @mode 2 selects mode 2.
abc.puckettespaf~.function: Generates phase-aligned formant tones, useful for vowel-like sounds.

abc.quadriout~.category: Audio I/O: hardware inputs, outputs & audio settings
abc.quadriout~.function: Sends a four-channel mc cord to chosen outputs with gain and meters.

abc.rev4~.builtin_alternative: abl.device.reverb~ — Ableton plate reverb with more detailed controls.
abc.rev4~.comments: Parameters use 0-127 scales, not seconds or dB. An @mode other than stereo or quadri fails to build the inner object.
abc.rev4~.function: Adds stereo or four-channel feedback-delay reverberation.

abc.rissetsbell~.comments: Trust the help patch over the refpage for the detune parameter name.
abc.rissetsbell~.function: Synthesises Risset's inharmonic bell on 11 output channels.

abc.scope.builtin_alternative: scope~ — built-in X-Y oscilloscope, no positive/negative colouring.
abc.scope.function: Displays an ambisonic scope in a floating OpenGL window.

abc.scopeembedded.builtin_alternative: scope~ — built-in X-Y oscilloscope, no positive/negative colouring.
abc.scopeembedded.comments: The usual choice for a presentation view; abc.scope opens a separate window.
abc.scopeembedded.function: Displays an ambisonic scope inside the patch.

abc.simplefmburst~.comments: Its refpage file declares the name abc.simpleburstfm~, which is not the object's name.
abc.simplefmburst~.function: Plays a short fixed FM burst when banged, as a test sound.

abc.soundcoat~.function: Generates an evolving noise texture from 16 randomly weighted filters.

abc.sounddetector~.builtin_alternative: thresh~ — detects a signal above a level, without separate attack and release pulses.
abc.sounddetector~.comments: noteDur, offDur and tSlide are undocumented beyond their ranges.
abc.sounddetector~.function: Detects note attacks and releases in an incoming signal.

abc.soundgrain~.comments: Plain Max patch, not a wrapper. Loads rainstick.aif from Max's own media folder into buffers with fixed global names (zaza, livegrain), shared by every instance.
abc.soundgrain~.function: Granulates a looped rainstick sample as a ready-made test texture.

abc.stereoout~.builtin_alternative: mc.dac~ — with mc.live.gain~ before it for level and metering.
abc.stereoout~.category: Audio I/O: hardware inputs, outputs & audio settings
abc.stereoout~.function: Sends a two-channel mc cord to outputs 1-2 with gain and meters.

abc.trajectories~.comments: Its refpage says it outputs cartesian coordinates, but the wrapper adds a polar conversion inside, and the help patches feed it straight into abc.hoa.map~. Numeric first argument does nothing; use @mode.
abc.trajectories~.function: Generates signal-rate 2D motion paths to drive ambisonic source positions.

abc.vbap~.comments: 2D only. Max has no built-in VBAP or multi-speaker panner, so this fills a real gap. Send a<i> for every speaker so the angles match the real layout.
abc.vbap~.function: Pans a mono source around an irregular speaker ring using VBAP.

abc.vector~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
abc.vector~.comments: An analysis and teaching tool, not a sound process. The ambisonic tutorial patch shows how to plot its output.
abc.vector~.function: Computes Gerzon energy and velocity vectors for a speaker setup.

_av.automation~.function: Internal panel used by av.automation~; not meant to be typed directly.

av.ampgate~.builtin_alternative: thresh~ — hard gate on the raw signal, no hold or ramps
av.ampgate~.comments: Built on av.follow~; has hold, attack and release times. Good for making visuals appear when sound starts.
av.ampgate~.function: Opens a smooth gate signal while audio stays above a dB threshold.

av.amp~.builtin_alternative: peakamp~ — peak level per interval, no smoothing
av.amp~.comments: Outputs a signal, or a float when banged (for example by jit.world's render bang).
av.amp~.function: Follows a signal's loudness with attack and release times in ms.

av.automation~.builtin_alternative: function — draw the curve, drive it yourself
av.automation~.comments: Locked to the global or a named transport. The typed box is replaced by a bpatcher.
av.automation~.function: Draws an automation curve that plays over a min:sec:ms length.

av.bfg.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.bfg with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.bfg.function: Creates a jit.gl.bfg preset that renders a simplex-noise texture.

av.camera.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.camera with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.camera.function: Creates a jit.gl.camera preset looking at the origin.

av.camera.control.comments: Keys a/s/d/w/q/z move, j/k/l/i pan, so no mouse is needed on stage. Positions work with pattrstorage presets.
av.camera.control.function: Moves a GL camera with keyboard and mouse and stores positions.

av.camera.drive.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.anim.drive with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.camera.drive.function: Creates a jit.anim.drive preset for keyboard and mouse camera moves.

av.catch~.function: Captures three audio signals into a 3-plane matrix, like a 3D scope.

av.chance.builtin_alternative: random with < — the same test in two objects
av.chance.comments: Default is 50%. Pairs well with av.trigger~.
av.chance.function: Passes a bang through with a set percent probability.

av.cornerpin.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.cornerpin with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.cornerpin.function: Creates a jit.gl.cornerpin preset with visible corner handles.

av.cross3~.function: Splits audio into low, mid and high bands at set crossover frequencies.

av.enable.comments: The right outlet feeds the effect; the left outlet bypasses it (refpage).
av.enable.function: Turns a jit.gl.pix or jit.gl.slab effect on or off with a toggle.

av.enable.xfade.comments: The processed texture must be fed back through this object. Uses cosine easing.
av.enable.xfade.function: Crossfades between a dry texture and a shader effect's output.

av.environment.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.environment with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.environment.function: Creates a jit.gl.environment preset for skyboxes and PBR lighting.

av.follow3~.comments: Built from av.cross3~ and av.follow~. Bang for a list, or use the three signal outlets.
av.follow3~.function: Follows the loudness of low, mid and high bands separately.

av.follow~.comments: Bang it to get a float, for example from jit.world's render bang.
av.follow~.function: Envelope follower with fast and slow followers and band filters for transients.

av.function.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for function with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.function.function: Creates a function preset with a grid and simple output settings.

av.grab.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.grab with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.grab.function: Creates a jit.grab preset that outputs camera input as a texture.

av.gridshape.cube.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.gridshape with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.gridshape.cube.function: Creates a lit jit.gl.gridshape cube preset.

av.gridshape.plane.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.gridshape with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.gridshape.plane.function: Creates an unlit jit.gl.gridshape plane preset.

av.gridshape.sphere.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.gridshape with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.gridshape.sphere.function: Creates a lit jit.gl.gridshape sphere preset.

av.gridshape.torus.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.gridshape with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.gridshape.torus.function: Creates a lit jit.gl.gridshape torus preset.

av.hidecursor.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
av.hidecursor.comments: Keeps the cursor off the projected window during a show.
av.hidecursor.function: Hides the mouse cursor after it has been idle for a set time.

av.light.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.light with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).

av.light.point.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.light with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).

av.light.shadows.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.light with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt). Pair with av.pbr.shadows.
av.light.shadows.function: Creates a directional jit.gl.light preset with shadows on.

av.loadbang.builtin_alternative: loadbang — can fire before attributes and presets have loaded
av.loadbang.function: Sends a bang after the whole patch has finished loading.

av.loadmess.builtin_alternative: loadmess — can fire before attributes and presets have loaded
av.loadmess.function: Sends a message after the whole patch has finished loading.

av.mesh.grid.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.mesh with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.mesh.grid.function: Creates a jit.gl.mesh preset that draws points as a wire grid.

av.mesh.lines.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.mesh with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.mesh.lines.function: Creates a jit.gl.mesh preset that draws connected lines.

av.mesh.points.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.mesh with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.mesh.points.function: Creates a jit.gl.mesh preset that draws round points.

av.midside~.comments: Useful before analysis, for example following the side signal's level.
av.midside~.function: Splits a stereo signal into mid and side signals.

av.movie.builtin_alternative: jit.movie — default engine, matrix output by default
av.movie.comments: Loads the start and end into RAM for seamless loops. Use av.movie~ when you need the sound.
av.movie.function: Plays a movie as a looping texture with the sound muted.

av.movieplay~.comments: Signal sets position in ms; wrap and fold modes allow looping. Render with a bang; cache defaults to 1 GB.
av.movieplay~.function: Plays a movie at a position set by an audio signal, like play~.

av.movie~.comments: Uses the VIDDLL engine; loads the start and end into RAM for seamless loops.
av.movie~.function: Plays a movie as a looping texture with stereo audio outputs.

av.node.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.node with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.node.function: Creates a jit.gl.node preset that renders a sub-scene to a texture.

av.noisiness~.comments: High-pitched tones also read as noisy.
av.noisiness~.function: Estimates how noisy a sound is, from 0 to 1, using zero crossings.

av.paramgenerator.comments: Alt/Option+Shift+click the slab object to generate them.
av.paramgenerator.function: Creates number boxes for a jit.gl.slab shader's parameters.

av.pbr.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.pbr with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt).
av.pbr.function: Creates a basic jit.gl.pbr material preset.

av.pbr.shadows.comments: A typed-name mapping: Max swaps the box for jit.gl.pbr with preset attributes (init/av-objectmappings.txt). Pair with av.light.shadows.
av.pbr.shadows.function: Creates a jit.gl.pbr material preset tuned for shadows.

av.phasor~.builtin_alternative: phasor~ — lock attribute syncs to transport, set by frequency or note value
av.phasor~.function: Transport-locked phasor~ whose cycle length is set in min:sec:ms.

av.pitch~.comments: Works best on a dry, monophonic signal. Holds the last pitch below the threshold.
av.pitch~.function: Tracks pitch as a 0–1 value and a MIDI float, with instrument ranges.

av.pix.alpha.add.function: Uses a second texture as the alpha channel of the first.

av.pix.alpha.remove.function: Makes a texture fully opaque and outputs its old alpha separately.

av.pix.blend.builtin_alternative: jit.fx.co.screen and the other jit.fx.co.* objects — one mode each
av.pix.blend.function: Blends two textures with a selectable blend mode.

av.pix.brcosa.comments: Has an on/off switch built in (uses av.enable inside).
av.pix.brcosa.function: Adjusts a texture's brightness, contrast and saturation.

av.pix.chromakey.builtin_alternative: jit.fx.co.chromakey — keys against a second input
av.pix.chromakey.comments: Outputs one texture with the key in its alpha channel, ready for layering.
av.pix.chromakey.function: Keys out a chosen color and makes it transparent.

av.pix.degrade.function: Pixelates a texture and reduces its color depth.

av.pix.delay.function: Delays a texture by a number of frames.

bach.rot.function: Rotates the elements of an llll and optionally its sublists.

bach.round.function: Rounds numbers in an llll to multiples of a value.

bach.scale.function: Maps numbers in an llll from one range to another.

bach.score.comments: The most capable notation editor for Max; heavy object with a long learning curve. Pair with bach.quantize for input from proportional data.
bach.score.function: Displays, edits and plays a multi-voice score in classical measured notation.

bach.score2roll.comments: Feed it bach.score's output after a score2roll message.
bach.score2roll.function: Converts bach.score content into bach.roll content, keeping markers.

crossref: Lists & data: sorting, shuffling & set operations
bach.scramble.function: Shuffles an llll into a random order.

bach.shelf.comments: Lets coll, dict or umenu refer to lllls by symbol; @embed saves contents with the patch.
bach.shelf.function: Stores many lllls under names and retrieves them by name.

bach.sieve.category: bach lllls: sorting, searching & lambda functions
bach.sieve.function: Keeps only the llll elements that pass a comparison or lambda test.

bach.skewness.function: Computes the skewness of the numbers in an llll.

bach.slice.function: Splits an llll in two at a given position.

bach.sliceheader.function: Separates the header from the note content of a score dump.

bach.slot.comments: Used for per-note data templates and envelope editing.
bach.slot.function: Shows and edits one slot window, such as an envelope, outside a score.

bach.slot2curve.comments: Plays per-note envelopes from bach scores through MSP.
bach.slot2curve.function: Converts a function slot into curve~ messages.

bach.slot2filtercoeff.function: Converts a dynfilter slot into line~ messages for filtercoeff~.

bach.slot2function.function: Converts a function slot into messages for a Max function object.

bach.slot2line.comments: Segment curvature is dropped; use bach.slot2curve to keep it.
bach.slot2line.function: Converts a function slot into line~ messages.

bach.sort.category: bach lllls: sorting, searching & lambda functions
bach.sort.comments: Second outlet gives the sorted indices.
bach.sort.function: Sorts an llll by default order or a lambda-loop comparison.

bach.split.function: Splits an llll into bracketed chunks at a separator element.

bach.stdev.function: Computes the standard deviation of the numbers in an llll.

bach.step.comments: Walks nested levels depth-first; bach.drip does the same on a timer.
bach.step.function: Outputs llll elements one at a time on each bang.

bach.stream.function: Keeps an llll of the last N elements received.

bach.submatrix.function: Extracts a rectangular part of a matrix llll.

bach.subs.function: Replaces or removes elements at given addresses of an llll.

bach.sum.function: Adds together all numbers in an llll.

bach.swap.function: Swaps two elements of an llll given their addresses.

bach.symdiff.function: Returns elements that are in either of two lllls but not both.

bach.textin.function: Parses text into an llll, choosing what to take literally.

bach.textout.function: Formats llll text output, controlling backticks and escaping.

bach.thin.category: bach lllls: sorting, searching & lambda functions
bach.thin.function: Removes duplicate elements from an llll.

bach.tierev.function: Reverses a sequence of ties correctly when reversing music.

bach.times.function: Multiplies lllls or numbers element by element.

bach.toc&r.function: Separates elements into chord and rest groups using a durations llll.

bach.tonnetz.category: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
bach.tonnetz.comments: Interactive harmony explorer; select nodes to form chords.
bach.tonnetz.function: Shows and edits pitches on a Tonnetz lattice built from two intervals.

bach.trace.comments: Not a debugging tap despite the name.
bach.trace.function: Computes the trace, the sum of the diagonal, of a matrix.

bach.trans.comments: Transposes in the matrix sense, not the pitch sense.
bach.trans.function: Swaps rows and columns of a nested llll, like a matrix transpose.

bach.transcribe.comments: Writes into bach.roll only; quantize afterwards for bach.score.
bach.transcribe.function: Records incoming notes into a bach.roll in real time.

bach.tree.comments: Good for seeing nested structure while learning bach.
bach.tree.function: Displays and edits an llll as a clickable tree diagram.

bach.union.function: Merges two lllls into their set union.

bach.unpacknote.function: Splits one note of score playback into pitch, velocity, duration and extras.

bach.urn.comments: Bangs a separate outlet when empty.
bach.urn.function: Picks random elements from an llll without repeating any.

bach.value.comments: Help file says this is safer than send and receive for passing lllls.
bach.value.function: Shares an llll among all same-named bach.value objects and bell variables.

bach.variance.function: Computes the variance of the numbers in an llll.

bach.weights.comments: Pairs well with nodes weights for 2D interpolation.
bach.weights.function: Blends several lllls as a weighted combination.

bach.wellshape.function: Pads matrix rows so the matrix becomes properly rectangular.

bach.wordcloud.function: Displays an interactive word cloud with sizes from weights.

bach.wrandom.comments: One of the simplest weighted-choice objects in Max if bach is installed.
bach.wrandom.function: Picks random elements from a pool using probability weights.

bach.wrap.function: Wraps an llll in extra brackets to add nesting levels.

bach.write.function: Saves an llll to a file on disk.

crossref: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
bach.writesdif.function: Writes an llll out as an SDIF analysis file.

bach.wurn.function: Picks weighted random elements from an llll without repeats.

bach.x2dx.function: Computes differences between neighboring elements, such as onsets into durations.

bach.zsearch.category: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
bach.zsearch.function: Finds families of Z-related pitch-class sets.

cage.agogics.function: Repeats a musical cell with accelerando or rallentando.

cage.arpeggio.function: Lists the notes of a chord pattern across a pitch range, in midicents.

cage.cascade~.comments: Works on bach.roll or bach.score data, not audio, despite the tilde.
cage.cascade~.function: Changes note velocities in a score as if passed through biquad filters.

cage.chain.comments: Requires bach. No built-in L-system object in Max.
cage.chain.function: Rewrites symbol sequences by grammar rules, for L-systems and 1D automata.

cage.chordinterp.function: Interpolates between several chords, adding voices where needed.

cage.chroma.fromcentroid.category: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
cage.chroma.fromcentroid.function: Finds a chroma vector that has a given tonal centroid.

cage.chroma.frompcset.category: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
cage.chroma.frompcset.function: Converts a pitch-class set with velocities into a chroma vector.

cage.chroma.tocentroid.category: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
cage.chroma.tocentroid.function: Computes the tonal centroid of a chroma vector.

cage.chroma.topcset.category: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
cage.chroma.topcset.function: Converts a chroma vector into pitch classes and velocities above a threshold.

cage.closer.function: Moves pitches by octaves to sit closest to a reference pitch.

cage.combinevoices.comments: Just calls bach.combinevoices; use that directly.
cage.combinevoices.function: Merges several roll or score contents into one multi-voice score.

cage.crop.comments: Requires bach. Replaces the old name cage.extract.
cage.crop.function: Extracts a time portion of a bach.roll or bach.score.

cage.dynamics.function: Compresses, expands or limits score velocities like an audio compressor.

cage.envelopes.comments: Requires bach. Needs several feedback connections to bach.roll or bach.score and bach.slot.
cage.envelopes.function: Reshapes score chords using envelopes drawn in a bach.slot.

cage.explodevoices.function: Moves score chords into different voices according to slot content.

cage.ezptrack.function: Connects neighboring notes in a bach.roll, like partial tracking.

cage.ezsampler~.comments: Requires bach. Quick way to sequence samples from a score.
cage.ezsampler~.function: Plays sound files stored in bach score slots during playback.

cage.ezsynth~.comments: Requires bach. Quick way to hear microtonal or spectral scores.
cage.ezsynth~.function: Plays bach score slot curves through an additive synthesizer.

cage.fm.comments: Requires bach. Symbolic: outputs notes, not audio.
cage.fm.function: Computes the note spectrum of frequency modulation between chords or scores.

cage.freqshift.function: Shifts all pitches of a score by a fixed amount in Hertz.

cage.granulate.function: Granulates a bach.roll symbolically in real time into another roll.

cage.harmser.function: Lists the harmonic series of a fundamental, with optional stretch, in midicents.

cage.inv.function: Inverts all pitches of a roll or score upside down.

cage.join.function: Joins several rolls or scores end to end.

cage.length.comments: Requires bach. For bach.score also gives measures and symbolic units.
cage.length.function: Reports the duration of a roll or score.

cage.life.comments: Requires bach. dada.life offers an interactive version.
cage.life.function: Evolves a 2D grid by cellular automaton rules set in a lambda loop.

cage.looper.function: Repeats a portion of a bach.roll, optionally changing each loop.

cage.lumbricus.function: Chains cells from weighted families into a sequence under lambda rules.

cage.markov.analysis.function: Builds Markov transition tables of a chosen order from incoming states.

cage.markov.synthesis.comments: Requires bach. Bangs an outlet when stuck.
cage.markov.synthesis.function: Generates new states from a Markov transition table.

cage.meta.engine.comments: Requires bach. Use with cage.meta.header inside each assigned patch; powerful but complex.
cage.meta.engine.function: Assigns a patch instance to each score note and controls it.

cage.meta.header.function: Receives note data inside a patch driven by cage.meta.engine.

cage.mix.function: Mixes several scores together into one.

cage.noterandom.function: Outputs random MIDI notes from a pitch grid with probability weights.

cage.notewalk.function: Outputs a random walk of MIDI notes within a pitch grid.

cage.offset.comments: Requires bach. Also typed as cage.shift.
cage.offset.function: Inserts or deletes time at the start of a roll or score.

cage.pitchfilter.function: Changes score velocities by a pitch filter drawn as a breakpoint function.

cage.profile.filter.function: Smooths or filters a melodic line of pitches.

cage.profile.gen.function: Generates a melodic line by sampling a pitch breakpoint function.

cage.profile.mirror.function: Mirrors a melodic line around a fixed pitch.

cage.profile.perturb.function: Adds random deviations to each pitch of a melodic line.

cage.profile.rectify.function: Folds pitches back inside a pitch range by reflection.

cage.profile.snap.function: Snaps a melodic line to a pitch grid.

cage.profile.stretch.function: Stretches a melodic line around a center pitch.

cage.rebar.function: Rewrites the meters and barlines of a bach.score.

cage.remapvoices.function: Reorders, removes, duplicates or merges the voices of a roll or score.

cage.repeat.function: Repeats a roll or score a number of times.

cage.rev.function: Reverses a roll or score in time.

cage.rhythminterp.comments: Requires bach. Refpage digest wrongly says chords.
cage.rhythminterp.function: Interpolates between rhythms, outputting onsets and durations.

cage.rm.comments: Requires bach. Symbolic: outputs notes, not audio.
cage.rm.function: Computes the note spectrum of ring modulation between chords or scores.

cage.rot.function: Rotates the content of a bach.roll circularly in time.

cage.scale.function: Lists the notes of a scale across a pitch range, in midicents.

cage.sdif.chordseq.pack.function: Packs chord-sequence analysis parameters into an SDIF llll.

cage.sdif.chordseq.toroll.comments: Requires bach; read the file with bach.readsdif.
cage.sdif.chordseq.toroll.function: Imports a chord-sequence SDIF analysis into bach.roll.

cage.sdif.chordseq.unpack.function: Unpacks chord-sequence SDIF analysis into separate parameter lllls.

cage.sdif.fzero.pack.function: Packs fundamental-frequency analysis parameters into an SDIF llll.

cage.sdif.fzero.toroll.comments: Requires bach; read the file with bach.readsdif.
cage.sdif.fzero.toroll.function: Imports a fundamental-frequency SDIF analysis into bach.roll.

cage.sdif.fzero.unpack.function: Unpacks fundamental-frequency SDIF analysis into separate parameter lllls.

cage.sdif.markers.fromroll.function: Exports bach.roll markers as an SDIF markers llll.

cage.sdif.markers.pack.function: Packs marker analysis parameters into an SDIF llll.

cage.sdif.markers.toroll.function: Imports an SDIF markers analysis as bach.roll markers.

cage.sdif.markers.unpack.function: Unpacks SDIF markers analysis into separate parameter lllls.

cage.sdif.peaks.pack.function: Packs spectral peak analysis parameters into an SDIF llll.

cage.sdif.peaks.toroll.comments: Requires bach; read the file with bach.readsdif.
cage.sdif.peaks.toroll.function: Imports a spectral peaks SDIF analysis into bach.roll as notes.

cage.sdif.peaks.unpack.function: Unpacks spectral peaks SDIF analysis into separate parameter lllls.

cage.sdif.ptrack.assemble.function: Assembles per-partial data into a partial-tracking SDIF llll.

cage.sdif.ptrack.pack.function: Packs partial-tracking analysis parameters into an SDIF llll.

cage.sdif.ptrack.resolve.function: Splits a partial-tracking SDIF analysis into per-partial data.

cage.sdif.ptrack.toroll.comments: Requires bach; read the file with bach.readsdif.
cage.sdif.ptrack.toroll.function: Imports a partial-tracking SDIF analysis into bach.roll, one note per partial.

cage.sdif.ptrack.unpack.function: Unpacks partial-tracking SDIF analysis into separate parameter lllls.

cage.separatevoices.function: Splits a roll or score into one roll or score per voice.

cage.shift.comments: Hidden alias of cage.offset kept for old patches.
cage.shift.function: Inserts or deletes time at the start of a roll or score.

cage.slice.function: Splits a bach.roll into time segments.

cage.spacer.function: Inserts silent time into a bach.roll at given positions.

cage.stretch.function: Stretches the pitches of a score in pitch or frequency space.

cage.timestretch.function: Stretches a roll or score in time by a fixed factor.

cage.timewarp.function: Distorts the timing of a roll by a function or markers.

cage.tonnetz.flip.category: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
cage.tonnetz.flip.function: Flips Tonnetz coordinates horizontally or vertically.

cage.tonnetz.rot.category: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory

cage.transp.function: Transposes all pitches of a roll or score.

cage.trim.function: Removes empty time at the start or end of a roll or score.

cage.virtfund.function: Computes virtual fundamentals of chords, rolls or scores.

cage.volume.function: Scales, offsets or windows all velocities in a roll or score.

cage.wedge.function: Inserts one bach.roll into another at given time positions.

cage.weightbuilder.function: Builds probability weights for pitches from a density function.

camu.analysis.comments: Args: corpus, audio track, descriptor track. Loads a camu.process.<choice> patch as a bpatcher.
camu.analysis.function: Chooses an analysis and segmentation method and shows its settings.

camu.cont.comments: Connect to mubu.concat~'s rightmost outlet; the concat~ needs @outputstate 1.
camu.cont.function: Keeps mubu.concat~ looping continuously in cont trigger mode.

camu.content-summary.comments: Args: corpus, audio track, descriptor track. Feed it camu.analysis output so it updates on load. Output as list, short or long text.
camu.content-summary.function: Reports how many files, segments and minutes of audio a corpus holds.

camu.control.blocks.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
camu.control.blocks.comments: Uses the blocks.pad and blocks.jit.matrix externals, which are not installed here.
camu.control.blocks.function: Plays a CataRT corpus from a ROLI Lightpad Block and displays it on the pad.

camu.control.linnstrument.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
camu.control.linnstrument.comments: Switches the LinnStrument to user firmware mode.
camu.control.linnstrument.function: Plays a CataRT corpus from a LinnStrument and lights the pads.

camu.control.mpe.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
camu.control.mpe.comments: Built around the Sensel Morph MPE overlay; other MPE controllers need the same controller layout.
camu.control.mpe.function: Turns MPE controller touches into CataRT touch messages.

camu.control.qwerty.category: Gesture & hardware: computer keyboard, mouse & game controllers
camu.control.qwerty.comments: Useful for testing touch-driven CataRT patches without a controller.
camu.control.qwerty.function: Turns computer-keyboard presses into CataRT touch messages.

camu.control.sensel.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
camu.control.sensel.comments: Uses the sensel external, which is not installed here.
camu.control.sensel.function: Turns Sensel Morph touches into CataRT touch messages.

camu.filenamenotenumber.comments: Lets a corpus be matched or transposed by the note named in each file.
camu.filenamenotenumber.function: Reads MIDI note numbers from sound file names into a descriptor column.

camu.imubu.control.function: Connects an imubu corpus display to selection and triggering.

camu.key.select.comments: Works with tags from camu.key.value or camu.key.soundset.
camu.key.select.function: Turns tagged groups of corpus sound files on or off.

camu.key.soundset.function: Tags corpus sound files automatically by their folder names.

camu.key.value.function: Tags corpus sound files with your own key-value labels.

camu.menu.function: Assigns a descriptor to a display parameter like x, y or colour.

camu.random.builtin_alternative: urn (random without repeats, no match lists)
camu.random.function: Picks one match from several nearest candidates by a random strategy.

camu.random.filter.function: Picks random matches only while the cursor is moving.

camu.record.comments: Left inlet record on/off, right inlet audio. Segmentation comes from the analysis it feeds (mubu.process / camu.analysis), not from camu.record itself.
camu.record.function: Records live audio into a corpus so it can be analyzed and played while recording.

camu.select.comments: Contains mubu.knn, camu.random.filter, camu.cont and camu.triggermode.
camu.select.function: Handles targets, nearest-match search and trigger modes for one voice.

camu.taboo.function: Blocks recently played segments from being chosen again for a while.

camu.target.function: Formats descriptor targets and column choices for mubu.knn.

camu.triggermode.comments: Modes: bow, fence, beat, beatmove, loop, loopmove, cont, contclick, click.
camu.triggermode.function: Chooses how cursor movement triggers corpus grains.

camu.voice.comments: Args: corpus, descriptor track. Load as a bpatcher to see its UI; use several for polyphony.
camu.voice.function: Plays one corpus voice built on mubu.concat~, with standard controls.

cv.jit.HSflow.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.HSflow.comments: The file is named cv.jit.HSflow. Grayscale char input; outputs 2-plane float32 flow. Use @unique 1 upstream so repeated frames do not zero the flow. Works best on small matrices.
cv.jit.HSflow.function: Computes dense optical flow with the Horn-Schunck method.

cv.jit.LKflow.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.LKflow.comments: The file is named cv.jit.LKflow. Grayscale char input; outputs 2-plane float32 flow. radius 1-7 trades quality for CPU. Use @unique 1 upstream. Works best on small matrices.
cv.jit.LKflow.function: Computes optical flow with the Lucas-Kanade method.

cv.jit.binedge.comments: 1-plane input; any non-zero pixel counts as on. Used inside cv.jit.perimeter.
cv.jit.binedge.function: Keeps only the edge pixels of shapes in a binary image.

cv.jit.blobs.bounds.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.blobs.bounds.comments: Input must come from cv.jit.label @charmode 1. Output is a 4-plane float32 matrix: left, top, right, bottom per blob. cv.jit.blobs.bounds.draw overlays the boxes.
cv.jit.blobs.bounds.function: Outputs a bounding box for every labeled blob in an image.

cv.jit.blobs.centroids.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.blobs.centroids.comments: Input must come from cv.jit.label @charmode 1. Output is a 3-plane matrix: x, y, area per blob. The standard step for tracking several objects.
cv.jit.blobs.centroids.function: Outputs the center point and area of every labeled blob.

cv.jit.blobs.direction.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.blobs.direction.comments: Needs cv.jit.label @charmode 1 then cv.jit.blobs.moments upstream. Unlike cv.jit.blobs.orientation it tells the two ends apart. flip chooses the lighter or heavier end.
cv.jit.blobs.direction.function: Outputs which way each labeled blob points, from its moments.

cv.jit.blobs.elongation.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.blobs.elongation.comments: Needs cv.jit.label @charmode 1 then cv.jit.blobs.moments upstream. Near 0 means compact, higher means thin.
cv.jit.blobs.elongation.function: Measures how thin or line-like each labeled blob is.

cv.jit.blobs.moments.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.blobs.moments.comments: Input must come from cv.jit.label @charmode 1. Output is a 17-plane float32 matrix. Feeds the other cv.jit.blobs shape objects.
cv.jit.blobs.moments.function: Computes shape descriptors (moments and Hu invariants) for every labeled blob.

cv.jit.blobs.orientation.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.blobs.orientation.comments: Needs cv.jit.label @charmode 1 then cv.jit.blobs.moments upstream. Cannot tell which end is which; use cv.jit.blobs.direction for that.
cv.jit.blobs.orientation.function: Outputs the main-axis angle of each labeled blob.

cv.jit.blobs.recon.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.blobs.recon.comments: Needs cv.jit.blobs.moments upstream and a model file made with cv.jit.learn (loaded with read). Lower values mean closer matches. Example models for the letters A and M are included.
cv.jit.blobs.recon.function: Scores how closely each blob's shape matches a trained model.

cv.jit.blobs.sort.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.blobs.sort.comments: Needs label output (charmode 1) plus blob centroids or moments. threshold is the largest movement in pixels still counted as the same blob (default 10). Simple; can fail when blobs cross.
cv.jit.blobs.sort.function: Keeps blob labels consistent from frame to frame for simple tracking.

cv.jit.blur.comments: CPU matrix version; works on char, float32 and float64, not long. radius sets blur size; sigma 0 calculates it from radius. For display-only blur, a GPU texture blur is faster.
cv.jit.blur.function: Applies a Gaussian blur to a matrix.

cv.jit.calibration.comments: Needs a rigid printed chessboard; set the inner corner counts. Collects several views, then write saves the calibration file. Built on OpenCV.
cv.jit.calibration.function: Calibrates a camera's lens distortion from views of a printed chessboard.

cv.jit.canny.builtin_alternative: jit.sobel (gradient edges, not thin binary ones)
cv.jit.canny.comments: Grayscale char input only. threshold sets how many edges appear; keep range near its default of 10. Output is less pretty than Sobel but better for analysis such as cv.jit.hough.
cv.jit.canny.function: Finds thin one-pixel edges in a grayscale image (Canny method).

cv.jit.cartopol.comments: Abstraction; the matrix version of cartopol. Pairs with cv.jit.poltocar.
cv.jit.cartopol.function: Converts x and y matrices to amplitude and angle, cell by cell.

cv.jit.centroids.comments: Takes any 1-plane matrix. Best for tracking one bright object. Outputs -1 -1 for an empty image. cv.jit.centroids.draw overlays the point.
cv.jit.centroids.function: Outputs the center of mass and total mass of a grayscale image.

cv.jit.changetype.comments: Abstraction. Send type <name> to change the output type.
cv.jit.changetype.function: Changes a matrix's data type while keeping planes and dimensions.

cv.jit.circularity.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.circularity.comments: Abstraction; a perfect circle gives 1. Pixel aliasing can make squares score close to circles.
cv.jit.circularity.function: Measures how round a shape is from its area and perimeter.

cv.jit.close.comments: Abstraction. Single-plane char input. Common clean-up step before labeling blobs.
cv.jit.close.function: Fills small holes and gaps in a binary image (dilate then erode).

cv.jit.covariance.comments: Takes a 1-dimension float32 or float64 matrix per frame and accumulates; reset clears it. Used for statistical shape analysis.
cv.jit.covariance.function: Builds a covariance matrix from a stream of vectors.

cv.jit.dilate.comments: 1-plane matrices. Binary by default; @grayscale 1 takes the neighborhood maximum. mode picks square or cross neighborhood.
cv.jit.dilate.function: Grows bright regions in an image (morphological dilation).

cv.jit.direction.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.direction.comments: Abstraction. Unlike cv.jit.orientation it tells the two ends apart. flip chooses pointing toward the lighter or heavier side.
cv.jit.direction.function: Outputs which way a shape points, from cv.jit.moments output.

cv.jit.elongation.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.elongation.comments: Abstraction. Near 0 means compact; higher means line-like. For many blobs use cv.jit.blobs.elongation.
cv.jit.elongation.function: Measures how thin a shape is, from cv.jit.moments output.

cv.jit.erode.comments: 1-plane matrices. Binary by default; @grayscale 1 takes the neighborhood minimum. mode picks square or cross neighborhood.
cv.jit.erode.function: Shrinks bright regions and removes specks (morphological erosion).

cv.jit.extrema.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
cv.jit.extrema.function: Finds local peaks in a matrix, such as strong lines in a Hough space.

cv.jit.face.landmarks.comments: Needs face rectangles from cv.jit.faces plus the same grayscale image in the right inlet. Output: one row of 68 points per face. @normalize 1 gives 0-1 coordinates; set it on all related objects.
cv.jit.face.landmarks.function: Finds 68 facial landmark points (eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jaw) per face.

cv.jit.face.parts.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
cv.jit.face.parts.comments: Abstraction; connect cv.jit.face.landmarks to its inlet.
cv.jit.face.parts.function: Splits face landmark data into nine outputs such as eyes, lips and jaw.

cv.jit.face.rigidpoints.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
cv.jit.face.rigidpoints.comments: Abstraction; connect cv.jit.face.landmarks. Output matches the cv.jit.keypoints format, so draw it with cv.jit.keypoints.draw. Useful for head-pose work with cv.jit.unproject.
cv.jit.face.rigidpoints.function: Picks six face landmarks that stay still when expression changes.

cv.jit.faces.comments: Grayscale char input only (use jit.rgb2luma). Works best on small images; faces about 20 pixels wide or larger. Query nfaces with getnfaces. model picks one of four cascades. cv.jit.faces.draw overlays boxes.
cv.jit.faces.function: Detects frontal faces in a grayscale image and outputs their rectangles.

cv.jit.features.comments: Grayscale char input. threshold (0-1) sets strictness; distance sets spacing; roi with useroi limits the search area. precision 1 gives sub-pixel accuracy but is slower.
cv.jit.features.function: Finds corner-like feature points that are easy to track.

cv.jit.features2track.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
cv.jit.features2track.comments: Abstraction; wire it to cv.jit.track. The right inlet takes a rectangle to search in.
cv.jit.features2track.function: Finds good starting points and loads them into cv.jit.track.

cv.jit.findchessboardcorners.comments: Used for camera or projector calibration. Set the inner corner counts of your board. Outputs a 2-plane float32 list of corners.
cv.jit.findchessboardcorners.function: Finds the inner corners of a printed chessboard in a camera image.

cv.jit.findcontours.comments: Outputs a 3-plane matrix: x, y and contour index. The help draws them with jit.gl.mesh. Handy for turning silhouettes into vector lines.
cv.jit.findcontours.function: Traces outlines of shapes in a binary image as ordered point lists.

cv.jit.findhomography.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
cv.jit.findhomography.comments: Takes 1-plane float32 matrices of n columns by 2 rows, unlike cv.jit.getperspective's 2-plane format. Apply the result with cv.jit.perspective.
cv.jit.findhomography.function: Calculates a 3x3 perspective transform from four or more point pairs.

cv.jit.floodfill.comments: Binary char input. seed x y sets the starting pixel; nothing happens if that pixel is off. Good for picking one blob by clicking.
cv.jit.floodfill.function: Extracts the single connected shape that contains a chosen pixel.

cv.jit.framesub.builtin_alternative: jit.op @op absdiff (with a delayed copy), jit.fx.co.difference
cv.jit.framesub.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.framesub.comments: Abstraction. The simplest motion detector; threshold the result for a motion mask.
cv.jit.framesub.function: Outputs the difference between each frame and the previous one.

cv.jit.getperspective.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
cv.jit.getperspective.comments: Takes two 2-plane float32 matrices of 4 cells: source and destination points. Apply the result to points with cv.jit.perspective.
cv.jit.getperspective.function: Calculates a 3x3 perspective transform from four point pairs.

cv.jit.hough.comments: Feed it cv.jit.canny output. rho and theta set resolution. Use cv.jit.hough2lines to read lines out, or cv.jit.lines for the whole job in one object.
cv.jit.hough.function: Converts binary edges into a Hough space, where lines show up as peaks.

cv.jit.hough2lines.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
