cv.jit.hough2lines.comments: Abstraction; arguments are the source image width and height. Finds infinite lines, not segments. Same output format as cv.jit.lines, so cv.jit.lines.draw works.
cv.jit.hough2lines.function: Reads whole straight lines out of a Hough space.

cv.jit.iter.function: Outputs a matrix one row or one column at a time.

cv.jit.kalman.comments: Takes a list of floats, such as x y from a tracker. velocity_weight and acceleration_weight tune it; small values like 0.001 usually work best. Useful for any noisy sensor data.
crossref: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.kalman.function: Smooths noisy tracking values with a Kalman filter.

cv.jit.keypoints.comments: Grayscale char input. threshold usually 0.05-0.3; octaves sets scales. Outlet 0 is a 6-plane point matrix; outlet 1 holds descriptors for cv.jit.keypoints.match. @normalize 1 gives 0-1 coordinates.
cv.jit.keypoints.function: Finds distinctive feature points at several scales, with descriptors for matching.

cv.jit.keypoints.match.comments: Needs keypoints and descriptors from two cv.jit.keypoints. Pass matches to cv.jit.unproject to get position and rotation. Useful for simple image-marker tracking.
cv.jit.keypoints.match.function: Matches keypoints between a target image and a camera image.

cv.jit.label.comments: Required before any cv.jit.blobs object; use @charmode 1 for them. threshold drops blobs smaller than that area. mode 1 labels by size rank. Up to 255 blobs in char mode.
cv.jit.label.function: Gives each separate blob in a binary image its own number.

cv.jit.learn.comments: Usually fed cv.jit.moments output, but any fixed-length list works. Train in the right inlet; compare in the left. write and read save models for cv.jit.blobs.recon.
cv.jit.learn.function: Trains on example lists and scores new lists by similarity.

cv.jit.lines.comments: Runs Canny and Hough internally. threshold, sensitivity, resolution, gap and length tune it. cv.jit.lines.draw overlays results.
cv.jit.lines.function: Finds straight line segments in a grayscale image.

cv.jit.lowpass.builtin_alternative: slide (single values, smoothing in steps not Hz)
cv.jit.lowpass.comments: Abstraction; takes floats or lists, not matrices. Set cutoff in Hz; reset or clear restarts it.
cv.jit.lowpass.function: Smooths floats or lists with a low-pass filter set in Hz.

cv.jit.mass.comments: Help file says it is kept for older patches. For char input the sum is divided by 255.
cv.jit.mass.function: Adds up all pixel values; for binary images, counts the on pixels.

cv.jit.mean.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.mean.comments: Any type and planecount. Good for building a background image for background subtraction. Accurate on char data.
cv.jit.mean.function: Averages every pixel over all frames since the last reset.

cv.jit.module.presence.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.module.presence.comments: Copy it into a Max for Live MIDI Effect. lo tunes out background motion; hi sets full activity. Infrared cameras help in dark rooms.
cv.jit.module.presence.function: Max for Live module that turns camera motion into MIDI CC 1.

cv.jit.moments.comments: Any 1-plane matrix. Outputs 7 moments, 7 Hu invariants, centroid and mass. Feeds cv.jit.orientation, cv.jit.elongation, cv.jit.direction and cv.jit.learn.
cv.jit.moments.function: Computes shape descriptors, centroid and mass for a whole image.

cv.jit.noise.comments: Not an image noise generator. Arguments: count, then min and max (uniform) or mean and standard deviation (@mode 1). seed repeats sequences.
cv.jit.noise.function: Outputs random floats or lists with uniform or normal distribution.

cv.jit.notempty.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
cv.jit.notempty.comments: Abstraction; right outlet reports 1 or 0. Mostly used to filter cv.jit.faces, which outputs a dummy matrix when it finds nothing.
cv.jit.notempty.function: Passes a matrix only if it is not an 'empty' one-cell zero matrix.

cv.jit.open.comments: Abstraction. Single-plane char input. Common clean-up step before labeling blobs.
cv.jit.open.function: Removes small bright specks from a binary image (erode then dilate).

cv.jit.opticalflow.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.opticalflow.comments: Grayscale input. method picks farneback, block matching, Horn-Schunck or Lucas-Kanade. Outputs separate x and y float32 matrices. Use @unique 1 upstream. cv.jit.flow.draw visualizes flow.
cv.jit.opticalflow.function: Computes optical flow with a choice of four algorithms.

cv.jit.orientation.category: Computer vision: helpers for blobs & shapes
cv.jit.orientation.comments: Abstraction; angle in radians from 0 to pi. Cannot tell the two ends apart; use cv.jit.direction for that.
cv.jit.orientation.function: Outputs the main-axis angle of a shape, from cv.jit.moments output.

cv.jit.perimeter.function: Counts the edge pixels of shapes in a binary image.

cv.jit.perspective.category: Computer vision: helpers for points, faces & perspective
cv.jit.perspective.comments: Transforms points, not images. Left inlet: 2-plane float32 points; right inlet: matrix from cv.jit.getperspective or cv.jit.findhomography. To warp an image on screen use jit.gl.cornerpin instead.
cv.jit.perspective.function: Applies a 3x3 perspective transform to a matrix of point coordinates.

cv.jit.poltocar.comments: Abstraction; the matrix version of poltocar. Pairs with cv.jit.cartopol.
cv.jit.poltocar.function: Converts amplitude and angle matrices to x and y, cell by cell.

cv.jit.ravg.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.ravg.comments: alpha from 0 to 1: 1 is instant, lower values smooth more. Useful for adaptive background subtraction.
cv.jit.ravg.function: Keeps a running average of each pixel to smooth changes over time.

cv.jit.resize.builtin_alternative: jit.matrix (dim with interp, lower quality when shrinking)
cv.jit.resize.comments: size w h sets the output. Shrinking averages pixels instead of skipping them.
cv.jit.resize.function: Resizes a matrix with bicubic interpolation for smoother results.

cv.jit.shift.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.shift.comments: Grayscale char input; often a jit.chromakey mask. rect sets the start window. mode 1 (CAMShift) also adapts size and angle. Outputs window, rotated corners and mass. cv.jit.shift.draw overlays it.
cv.jit.shift.function: Tracks a bright region by moving a window with MeanShift or CAMShift.

cv.jit.stddev.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.stddev.comments: Abstraction; also outputs the mean. reset clears the history. Useful for spotting pixels that normally flicker.
cv.jit.stddev.function: Computes each pixel's standard deviation over time.

cv.jit.sum.builtin_alternative: jit.3m (per-plane mean; multiply by cell count)
cv.jit.sum.comments: Any type and planecount; outputs a list with one value per plane. Handy as an overall activity measure.
cv.jit.sum.function: Outputs the sum of all pixel values in each plane.

cv.jit.threshold.comments: Single-plane char input. radius sets the neighborhood; threshold sets the offset; mode picks the algorithm.
cv.jit.threshold.function: Thresholds an image against its local surroundings to handle uneven lighting.

cv.jit.touches.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.touches.comments: Abstraction built on MeanShift, made for touch surfaces. Binary char input on black. Three outlets list new, moving and lost objects as ID, x, y, radius. radius sets object size; reset restarts IDs.
crossref: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
cv.jit.touches.function: Tracks several bright blobs of similar size and gives each a lasting ID.

cv.jit.track.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.track.comments: Grayscale char input. npoints sets how many; set index x y places a point. Output plane 3 reports whether each point is still tracked. Seed points with cv.jit.features2track.
cv.jit.track.function: Follows chosen points from frame to frame using optical flow.

cv.jit.undergrad.comments: Abstraction; the help file points to cv.jit.learn as the more capable version. save and load store models.
cv.jit.undergrad.function: Trains on example lists and counts how many values match a new list.

cv.jit.unproject.comments: Right inlet: 3D model points; left: their 2D image positions (keypoints or face landmarks). Outputs translation and rotation for GL objects. Adjust focal distance if results look off.
cv.jit.unproject.function: Estimates 3D position and rotation from matching 2D image and 3D points.

cv.jit.variance.category: Computer vision: motion, tracking & optical flow
cv.jit.variance.comments: Abstraction; the help file recommends the easier cv.jit.stddev. reset clears the history.
cv.jit.variance.function: Computes each pixel's variance over time.

dada.analysis.centroid.function: Finds the average pitch, or pitch centroid, of a score.

crossref: Pitch & frequency: pitch-class sets & harmony theory
dada.analysis.chroma.function: Computes the chroma vector of a score.

dada.analysis.count.function: Counts the notes or chords in a score.

dada.analysis.duration.function: Reports the duration of a score in milliseconds.

dada.analysis.energy.function: Finds the average velocity of a score.

dada.analysis.minmax.function: Finds the minimum and maximum of a parameter in a score.

dada.analysis.rhythmdistrib.function: Computes how rhythmic energy is spread across a score.

dada.analysis.spread.function: Finds how widely pitches spread around the centroid in a score.

dada.base.comments: Requires bach. Can import CSV files; feeds dada.cartesian and dada.distances.
dada.base.function: Stores scores and ordinary Max data in an SQLite database queried with SQL.

dada.bodies.function: Plays notes as planets orbit and pass fixed stars in a gravity simulation.

dada.boids.comments: Requires bach. Good for gestural control data; rules like center, avoid and align.
dada.boids.function: Simulates a flock or swarm with editable rules and outputs positions.

dada.bounce.comments: Requires bach. Each wall can carry a pitch or a whole score.
dada.bounce.function: Bounces balls in a drawn 2D room, triggering notes on each wall hit.

dada.cartesian.comments: Requires bach and dada.base. Symbolic CataRT-style corpus explorer for score segments.
dada.cartesian.function: Plots database grains on 2D feature axes to browse and play by mouse.

dada.catart.function: Plots database grains on 2D feature axes to browse and play by mouse.

dada.distances.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
dada.distances.function: Places database items in 2D by their distances, using multidimensional scaling.

dada.graph.comments: Requires bach. Can walk the graph as a Markov chain.
dada.graph.function: Draws and edits a node-and-edge graph with automatic layout.

dada.kaleido.function: Plays notes from shapes moving in a kaleidoscope mirror chamber.

dada.life.function: Runs and displays 2D cellular automata that can play notes.

dada.life.info.function: Reports period, orbit and lifetime of a dada.life pattern.

dada.machines.comments: Requires bach. Custom machines are defined via lambda loops. Port counts unsettled: refpage says 1 in / 1 out, the help file's box shows 2 / 4.
dada.machines.function: Transforms scores or data through a drawn network of processing machines.

dada.multibrot.function: Displays Mandelbrot-style sets and reports divergence data for points.

dada.music~.comments: Mac only. A thought experiment more than a practical tool.
dada.music~.function: Browses a timeline that contains every possible short digital sound.

dada.nodes.function: Interpolates pitch and velocity between nodes placed in a 2D space.

dada.peanos~.comments: Requires bach. No help file ships.
dada.peanos~.function: Browses a space of static timbres and plays them.

dada.platform.comments: Requires bach. Saving level state is tricky; read the help file.
dada.platform.function: Builds scriptable platform-game levels whose events can trigger music.

dada.segment.comments: Requires bach. Feeds dada.base for corpus-based composition.
dada.segment.function: Cuts a bach.roll or bach.score into segments and computes their features.

dada.stage.comments: Requires bach. Display only; does no audio spatialization.
dada.stage.function: Shows movable icon cards with values on a 2D stage, like a mixer view.

dada.terrain.ellipse~.function: Generates x and y signals tracing a circle or ellipse.

dada.terrain.rect~.function: Generates x and y signals tracing a rectangle.

dada.terrain.segment~.function: Generates x and y signals tracing a straight line.

dada.terrain.spiral~.function: Generates x and y signals tracing a spiral.

dada.terrain~.comments: Requires bach. Terrain formula compiles on the fly and changes only with DSP off. Can also morph radially arranged buffers.
dada.terrain~.function: Synthesizes sound by reading a 2D terrain function along a signal path.

ears.!-~.comments: Needs the bach package. The file name ears.rminus~ also loads it.
ears.!-~.function: Subtracts buffer samples from a number, envelope or buffer.

ears.!/~.comments: Needs the bach package. The file name ears.rdiv~ also loads it.
ears.!/~.function: Divides a number, envelope or buffer by buffer samples.

ears.!=~.comments: Needs the bach package. The file name ears.neq~ also loads it.

ears.*~.comments: Needs the bach package. The file name ears.times~ also loads it.
ears.*~.function: Multiplies buffer samples by a number, envelope or buffer.

ears.+~.comments: Needs the bach package.  Adding two buffers mixes them. The file name ears.plus~ also loads it.
ears.+~.function: Adds a number, envelope or buffer to buffer samples.

ears.-~.comments: Needs the bach package. The file name ears.minus~ also loads it.
ears.-~.function: Subtracts a number, envelope or buffer from buffer samples.

ears./~.comments: Needs the bach package. The file name ears.div~ also loads it.
ears./~.function: Divides buffer samples by a number, envelope or other buffer.

ears.==~.comments: Needs the bach package.  Not an equalizer. The file name ears.eq~ also loads it.
ears.==~.function: Checks whether two buffers are identical.

ears.assemble~.comments: Needs the bach package. Builds a mix incrementally, useful with algorithmic timing.
ears.assemble~.function: Places incoming buffers one by one at set times into one output buffer.

crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.biquad~.function: Filters a buffer offline with a biquad filter.

ears.channel~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.channel~.function: Extracts chosen channels from a buffer into a new buffer.

ears.clicks~.comments: Needs the bach package. Handy for exporting click tracks.
ears.clicks~.function: Creates a buffer with clicks at given time points.

crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.clip~.function: Hard-clips the samples of a buffer offline.

ears.collect~.builtin_alternative: peek~ (writes single samples into an existing buffer~)
ears.collect~.category: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
ears.collect~.function: Builds a buffer from individual sample values sent as messages.

ears.cqt~.comments: Needs the bach package. Output is a buffer holding the spectrogram; view it with ears.specshow~.
ears.cqt~.function: Computes a constant-Q (musical pitch-spaced) spectrogram of a buffer.

ears.crop~.function: Keeps only a chosen time span of a buffer.

ears.dcfilter~.function: Removes DC offset from a buffer.

ears.delace~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.delace~.function: Splits interleaved channel data into separate channels.

ears.dynamics~.comments: Needs the bach package. Set thresh, ratio, attack, release, knee and makeup.
crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.dynamics~.function: Compresses the dynamics of a buffer offline.

ears.envelope~.builtin_alternative: buffer~ (fill message fills with a value or function)
ears.envelope~.function: Creates a buffer from a number or a breakpoint envelope.

ears.essentia~.category: Audio analysis: descriptor bundles & analysis frames
ears.essentia~.comments: Needs the bach package. Uses the Essentia library. Choose descriptors by argument; see the ears example patch 'Extract Audio Features'.
ears.essentia~.function: Extracts audio features such as pitch, loudness and onsets from a buffer.

ears.expr~.function: Applies a math expression to one or more buffers.

ears.fade~.comments: Needs the bach package. Curve shapes set per fade.
ears.fade~.function: Applies fade-ins and fade-outs to a buffer.

ears.fft~.comments: Needs the bach package. For frame-by-frame spectra use ears.stft~.
ears.fft~.function: Applies a single Fourier transform, or its inverse, to a whole buffer.

ears.filterempty~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.filterempty~.function: Passes on only buffers that are not empty.

ears.format~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.format~.function: Changes a buffer's channel count, duration or sample rate.

ears.freeverb~.comments: Needs the bach package. Use tail to leave room for the reverb to ring out.
crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.freeverb~.function: Adds Freeverb reverb to a buffer offline.

ears.fromdiffs~.category: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
ears.fromdiffs~.comments: Needs the bach package. Undoes ears.todiffs~.
ears.fromdiffs~.function: Rebuilds a buffer from sample or frame differences.

ears.fromsamps~.category: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
ears.fromsamps~.comments: Needs the bach package. Input is a bach llll.
crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
ears.fromsamps~.function: Creates a buffer from a list of sample values.

ears.fromvector~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.fromvector~.comments: Needs the bach package. Only works inside a patch loaded by ears.process~. Pair with ears.tovector~.
ears.fromvector~.function: Turns each signal vector into a list inside an ears.process~ patch.

ears.gain~.comments: Needs the bach package. Envelopes let you draw volume changes over time.
ears.gain~.function: Changes a buffer's gain by a number, envelope or buffer.

ears.griffinlim~.comments: Needs the bach package. More iterations sound cleaner but take longer.
ears.griffinlim~.function: Rebuilds audio from a magnitude-only spectrogram by estimating phases.

ears.hoa.decode~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
ears.hoa.decode~.function: Decodes ambisonic buffers to speakers or binaural stereo offline.

ears.hoa.encode~.category: Spatial audio: ambisonic encoding, decoding & binaural
ears.hoa.encode~.comments: Needs the bach package. Positions can change over time with envelopes.
ears.hoa.encode~.function: Pans buffers into higher-order ambisonic buffers offline.

ears.hoa.mirror~.function: Mirrors an ambisonic buffer along an axis.

ears.hoa.rotate~.function: Rotates the sound field of an ambisonic buffer.

ears.in.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.in.comments: Needs the bach package. Only used inside a patch loaded by ears.process~.
ears.in.function: Receives messages from the parent inside an ears.process~ patch.

ears.info~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.info~.function: Reports a buffer's duration, sample rate, channels and other details.

ears.interp~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.interp~.function: Creates buffers that step gradually between two buffers.

ears.in~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.in~.comments: Needs the bach package. Only used inside a patch loaded by ears.process~.
ears.in~.function: Brings buffer audio into a patch run by ears.process~.

ears.istft~.comments: Needs the bach package. Inverse of ears.stft~; settings should match.
ears.istft~.function: Turns a spectrogram buffer back into audio.

ears.iter~.category: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
ears.iter~.function: Outputs a buffer's samples one by one as messages.

ears.join~.comments: Needs the bach package. Set xfade for crossfades between pieces.
ears.join~.function: Joins buffers end to end, with optional crossfades.

ears.lace~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.lace~.function: Interleaves the channels of two buffers.

ears.mc.in~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.mc.in~.comments: Needs the bach package. Only used inside a patch loaded by ears.process~.
ears.mc.in~.function: Brings multichannel buffer audio into a patch run by ears.process~.

ears.mc.out~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.mc.out~.comments: Needs the bach package. Only used inside a patch loaded by ears.process~.
ears.mc.out~.function: Sends multichannel audio out of a patch run by ears.process~ into a buffer.

ears.mixdown~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.mixdown~.function: Mixes a buffer down to fewer channels.

ears.mix~.function: Mixes several buffers together, with offsets and gains.

ears.model.sine.analysis~.comments: Needs the bach package. Output feeds ears.model.sine.synthesis~ for resynthesis after editing.
ears.model.sine.analysis~.function: Analyses a buffer into tracked sine partials.

ears.model.sine.synthesis~.comments: Needs the bach package. Pair with ears.model.sine.analysis~.
ears.model.sine.synthesis~.function: Resynthesizes audio from sine partial data.

ears.model.sps.analysis~.comments: Needs the bach package. Pair with ears.model.sps.synthesis~.
ears.model.sps.analysis~.function: Analyses a buffer into sine partials plus a noise part.

ears.model.sps.synthesis~.comments: Needs the bach package. Pair with ears.model.sps.analysis~.
ears.model.sps.synthesis~.function: Resynthesizes audio from sine-plus-noise model data.

ears.model.stochastic.analysis~.comments: Needs the bach package. Pair with ears.model.stochastic.synthesis~.
ears.model.stochastic.analysis~.function: Analyses the noisy spectral envelope of a buffer.

ears.model.stochastic.synthesis~.function: Resynthesizes noise shaped by stochastic model data.

ears.normalize~.function: Scales a buffer so its peak or RMS reaches a target level.

ears.offset~.function: Adds or removes time at the start of a buffer.

crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.onepole~.function: Applies a gentle lowpass or highpass filter to a buffer.

ears.out.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.out.comments: Needs the bach package. Only used inside a patch loaded by ears.process~.
ears.out.function: Sends messages to the parent from inside an ears.process~ patch.

ears.out~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.out~.comments: Needs the bach package. Only used inside a patch loaded by ears.process~.
ears.out~.function: Sends audio out of a patch run by ears.process~ into a buffer.

crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.overdrive~.function: Soft-clips a buffer offline for distortion.

ears.pack~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.pack~.function: Combines separate buffers into one multichannel buffer.

ears.pan~.function: Pans a buffer across channels, optionally changing over time.

ears.paulfreeze~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.paulfreeze~.function: Freezes a moment of a buffer into a sustained sound with Paulstretch.

ears.paulstretch~.builtin_alternative: stretch~ (moderate time and pitch changes on a buffer~)
ears.paulstretch~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.paulstretch~.comments: Needs the bach package. Best for huge stretches and ambient textures; smears attacks.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
ears.paulstretch~.function: Time-stretches a buffer to extreme lengths with Paulstretch.

ears.peaks~.comments: Needs the bach package. Works on output of ears.stft~ or ears.cqt~.
ears.peaks~.function: Finds peaks in a spectrogram buffer.

ears.phaseunwrap~.function: Unwraps phase values in a buffer.

ears.phasewrap~.function: Wraps buffer values into the range minus pi to pi.

ears.playmp3~.comments: Needs the bach package. Not listed in ears' own object registry; the external exists but treat it as legacy.
ears.playmp3~.function: Plays sections of mp3 files without converting them first.

ears.processinfo~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.processinfo~.comments: Needs the bach package. Only used inside a patch loaded by ears.process~.
ears.processinfo~.function: Reports progress and state inside an ears.process~ patch.

ears.process~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.process~.comments: Needs the bach package. Like poly~ for offline rendering: the loaded patch uses ears.in~ and ears.out~. Experimental; objects that turn signals into messages can mistime.
ears.process~.function: Runs an ordinary MSP patch offline to process buffers faster than realtime.

ears.read~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.read~.comments: Needs the bach package. One buffer per file; accepts lists of files and drag and drop. Usually the first ears object in a chain.

ears.reg~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.reg~.function: Stores a buffer, or a copy of it, and outputs it on bang.

ears.repeat~.function: Loops a buffer a given number of times into a longer buffer.

ears.resample~.builtin_alternative: stretch~ (pitch and time changes on a buffer~)
ears.resample~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.resample~.function: Resamples a buffer, optionally changing its sample rate.

ears.roll.sampling~.comments: Needs the bach package. Notes must carry file or buffer names in slots.
ears.roll.sampling~.function: Renders a bach.roll of sound-file notes into a mixed buffer.

ears.roll.synthesis~.function: Renders a bach.roll into a buffer using simple oscillators per note.

ears.roll.toreaper~.function: Exports a bach.roll as a Reaper project with audio clips.

ears.rot~.function: Rotates a buffer's contents circularly in time.

ears.rubberband~.builtin_alternative: stretch~ (built-in pitch and time on a buffer~)
ears.rubberband~.category: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
ears.rubberband~.comments: Needs the bach package. High quality; can keep formants. Offline only.
crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.rubberband~.function: Time-stretches and pitch-shifts a buffer with Rubber Band.

ears.slice~.function: Cuts a buffer into two at a time point.

ears.soundtouch~.builtin_alternative: stretch~ (built-in pitch and time on a buffer~)
ears.soundtouch~.category: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
ears.soundtouch~.comments: Needs the bach package. Faster but usually lower quality than ears.rubberband~.
crossref: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.soundtouch~.function: Time-stretches and pitch-shifts a buffer with SoundTouch.

ears.specshow~.comments: Needs the bach package. Shows output of ears.stft~, ears.cqt~ or ears.tempogram~.
ears.specshow~.function: Displays a spectrogram buffer as an image.

ears.split~.comments: Needs the bach package. Set mode to choose the splitting rule.
crossref: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
ears.split~.function: Splits a buffer into many buffers by length, silence or attacks.

ears.stft~.comments: Needs the bach package. Edit the spectrogram, then return to audio with ears.istft~.
ears.stft~.function: Computes a spectrogram of a buffer, stored as a buffer.

ears.tempogram~.category: Audio analysis: slicing sound files & buffers
ears.tempogram~.function: Computes how tempo changes over time in a buffer.

ears.timesquash~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.timesquash~.comments: Needs the bach package. Content-aware resizing, like seam carving for audio.
crossref: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
ears.timesquash~.function: Shortens or lengthens a buffer while trying to keep important content.

ears.todiffs~.category: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
ears.todiffs~.function: Outputs differences between consecutive samples or frames.

ears.tosamps~.category: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
ears.tosamps~.comments: Needs the bach package. Output is a bach llll.
crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
ears.tosamps~.function: Outputs a buffer's samples as a list.

ears.tovector~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.tovector~.comments: Needs the bach package. Only works inside a patch loaded by ears.process~. Pair with ears.fromvector~.
ears.tovector~.function: Turns lists of numbers into signal vectors inside an ears.process~ patch.

ears.trans~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.trans~.function: Swaps a buffer's samples and channels, like transposing a matrix.

ears.trim~.comments: Needs the bach package. Set the silence level with thresh.
ears.trim~.function: Removes silence from the start and end of a buffer.

ears.unpack~.category: Buffers & offline: channels, sample rate & format
ears.unpack~.function: Splits a multichannel buffer into single-channel buffers.

ears.vamp~.category: Audio analysis: descriptor bundles & analysis frames
ears.vamp~.comments: Needs the bach package. Needs Vamp plug-ins installed on the computer.
ears.vamp~.function: Extracts audio features from a buffer using Vamp plug-ins.

ears.waveset.average~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.waveset.average~.comments: Needs the bach package. Trevor Wishart-style waveset distortion.
ears.waveset.average~.function: Averages neighbouring wavesets (segments between zero crossings) in a buffer.

ears.waveset.decimate~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.waveset.decimate~.function: Removes some wavesets from a buffer.

ears.waveset.interp~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.waveset.interp~.function: Morphs gradually between wavesets in a buffer.

ears.waveset.repeat~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.waveset.repeat~.comments: Needs the bach package. Classic waveset stretching effect; sounds glitchy on noisy material.
ears.waveset.repeat~.function: Repeats each waveset in a buffer several times.

ears.waveset.shuffle~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.waveset.shuffle~.function: Shuffles the order of wavesets in a buffer.

ears.waveset.split~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.waveset.split~.function: Splits a buffer into separate buffers at zero crossings.

ears.waveset.subs~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.waveset.subs~.function: Replaces each waveset with another waveform.

ears.window~.category: Buffers & offline: stretching, wavesets & offline effects
ears.window~.function: Applies an analysis window shape to a buffer.

ears.write~.category: Buffers & offline: loading, saving & offline processing
ears.write~.comments: Needs the bach package. Supports formats such as mp3 and flac and several files at once.

ease.comments: Official Cycling '74 package. Choose the curve by name or number. Drive it with line for eased motion.
ease.function: Reshapes numbers with a chosen easing curve, such as bounce or ease-in.

ease.xfade.comments: Send the target list, then a 0–1 position (e.g. from line). Good for moving several values at once.
ease.xfade.function: Moves smoothly from the last list to a new list along an easing curve.

ease.xfade~.comments: Driven by a 0–1 position signal. Useful for eased portamento and LFO shaping.
ease.xfade~.function: Crossfades between two signal values along an easing curve.

ease~.comments: syncupdate waits for the ramp to restart before changing the curve.
ease~.function: Reshapes a signal with an easing curve, e.g. to bend a phasor~ ramp.

jit.ease.comments: Can serve as a quick lookup table for shaping images or geometry.
jit.ease.function: Applies an easing curve to every cell of a Jitter matrix.

list.ease.function: Applies an easing curve to every number in a list.

ej.4m.comments: A js script (js ej.4m.js); the ejies readme marks it obsolete. Argument sets the window size.
ej.4m.function: Outputs min, median, mean and max over a sliding window of numbers.

ej.buffer2l.builtin_alternative: array.frombuffer (reads buffer values into an array)
ej.buffer2l.category: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
ej.buffer2l.comments: Type it as mxj ej.buffer2l. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Set the buffer with @buf_name.
crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
ej.buffer2l.function: Picks representative samples from a buffer~ as a list, for waveform drawing.

ej.cc.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
ej.cc.comments: A js script (js ej.cc.js). Written for older Max; its color handling predates Max 7 styles and themes. Optional argument turns off searching subpatchers.
ej.cc.function: Changes the colors of objects in a patch by their scripting name.

ej.cn.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
ej.cn.comments: A js script (js ej.cn.js). Send old name and new name as a list.
ej.cn.function: Renames an object's scripting name from inside the patch.

ej.cycle.builtin_alternative: cycle (splits list items across outlets instead)
ej.cycle.category: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
ej.cycle.comments: A js script (js ej.cycle.js N). Unlike cycle, it keeps messages with arguments intact. set chooses the next outlet.
ej.cycle.function: Sends each whole incoming message to the next outlet in turn.

ej.dialog.comments: Abstraction; arguments are the prompt text. Right outlet reports cancel or Escape.
ej.dialog.function: Opens a floating dialog box for typing text.

ej.dn.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
ej.dn.comments: A js script (js ej.dn.js). Place it at the top level of the main patch. Argument 1 matches partial names.
ej.dn.function: Opens the patcher window that holds a named object and shows it.

ej.dx2x.comments: Type it as mxj ej.dx2x. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Argument sets the origin. Inverse of ej.x2dx.
ej.dx2x.function: Turns a list of intervals into running totals from a starting value.

ej.fplay.comments: Type it as mxj ej.fplay. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Syncs with ej.function; uses the same messages.
ej.fplay.function: Stores and plays breakpoint functions without a display, like function without UI.

ej.ftom.builtin_alternative: ftom (has a base attribute and accepts lists)
ej.ftom.comments: Type it as mxj ej.ftom. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. @mode can round to semitones, quarter tones or 1/n tones.
ej.ftom.function: Converts frequencies to MIDI note numbers with custom tuning and rounding.

ej.function.comments: jsui object; add it from the object prototypes or snippets. Same messages as function plus curve mode, move modes, zoom and grid. Pair with ej.fplay (Java) for headless playback.
ej.function.function: Draws and edits several breakpoint functions in one display.

ej.jit.preview.comments: A bpatcher; create it from the bpatcher prototypes. Slowing the refresh saves CPU while monitoring.
ej.jit.preview.function: Shows a Jitter matrix in a small window with an adjustable refresh rate.

ej.l2buffer.builtin_alternative: array.tobuffer (writes array values to a buffer)
ej.l2buffer.category: Buffers & offline: buffer data as lists & SDIF
ej.l2buffer.comments: Type it as mxj ej.l2buffer. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. set <buffer> <channel> picks the destination.
crossref: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
ej.l2buffer.function: Writes a list of numbers into a buffer~ channel.

ej.lchange.category: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
ej.lchange.comments: Type it as mxj ej.lchange. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. mode 0 passes the list, 1 bangs, 2 outputs 1 or 0.
ej.lchange.function: Passes a list only when it differs from the previous one.

ej.lclip.comments: Type it as mxj ej.lclip. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Can also write results straight into a buffer~.
ej.lclip.function: Limits every number in a list to a minimum and maximum.

ej.ldrunk.comments: Type it as mxj ej.ldrunk. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Arguments: min, max, step, probability. interval makes it output continuously.
ej.ldrunk.function: Applies a random walk to every value in a list.

ej.led.category: UI: buttons, pads, tabs & color pickers
ej.led.comments: jsui object from the ejies prototypes or snippets. pict N changes its color.
ej.led.function: Shows an on/off light that can flash, as a button or toggle.

ej.line.comments: Abstraction. The help file notes timing drift as segment counts grow; a smaller grain reduces it. First argument sets start value and int or float output.
ej.line.function: Ramps through multiple segments at control rate with a set output interval.

ej.linterp.comments: Type it as mxj ej.linterp. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Can write results into a buffer~. @autotrigger makes each input update the output.
ej.linterp.function: Blends between up to eight stored lists by weights or a position.

ej.lock.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
ej.lock.comments: A js script (js ej.lock.js). Polling for lock changes is unreliable since Max 5 because a patcher can have several views.
ej.lock.function: Gets or sets whether the patcher window is locked.

ej.lop.comments: Type it as mxj ej.lop. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Arguments: operator then value(s), such as + 1. Includes atodb and dbtoa.
ej.lop.function: Applies math, comparison or trig operations to every item of long lists.

ej.lquant.comments: Type it as mxj ej.lquant. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Several quantize values can be given.
ej.lquant.function: Rounds each number in a list to the nearest multiple of a step.

ej.lscale.comments: Type it as mxj ej.lscale. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Arguments: in low, in high, out low, out high, exponent. @clip keeps output in range.
ej.lscale.function: Maps every number in a list from one range to another, with optional curve.

ej.lslide.comments: Type it as mxj ej.lslide. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Arguments set slide up and down. interval makes it output continuously.
ej.lslide.function: Smooths changes in every value of a list over time.

ej.lui.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
ej.lui.comments: A js script: type js ej.lui.js <file.js> in an object box. A typing shortcut from older Max versions.
ej.lui.function: Creates a jsui object from a script name, then deletes itself.

ej.mmmm.comments: Type it as mxj ej.mmmm. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Faster replacement for ej.4m. @mode list outputs all four as one list.
ej.mmmm.function: Outputs min, median, mean and max over a sliding window of numbers.

ej.mout~.comments: Abstraction; argument sets speaker count. @offset 0 puts position 0 on the first speaker instead of between the first two. Pans by reading a stored gain curve; no distance or height.
ej.mout~.function: Pans a mono signal around 2 to 16 speakers by position.

ej.mtof.builtin_alternative: mtof (has a base attribute and accepts lists)
ej.mtof.comments: Type it as mxj ej.mtof. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Arguments: tuning in Hz, reference MIDI note.
ej.mtof.function: Converts MIDI note numbers to frequencies with custom tuning.

ej.nthru.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
ej.nthru.comments: A js script (js ej.nthru.js <inlets> <outlets>). Useful only as a placeholder.
ej.nthru.function: Passes input through unchanged, with any number of inlets and outlets.

ej.numbox.comments: jsui object from the ejies prototypes or snippets. select gives it keyboard focus.
ej.numbox.function: A number box with Tab-key navigation, rounding and display options.

ej.op.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
ej.op.comments: A js script (js ej.op.js). Arguments allow partial and case-insensitive name matching.
ej.op.function: Opens a subpatcher window by its scripting name.

ej.route.comments: A js script (js ej.route.js). Outlets for bang, int, float, list, symbol and signal.
ej.route.function: Routes messages to different outlets by data type.

ej.sliders-overview.comments: A reference patch, not an object. The sliders are pictslider prototypes in an old macOS Aqua look.
ej.sliders-overview.function: Shows a gallery of Aqua-style picture slider designs you can copy.

ej.urn.comments: Type it as mxj ej.urn. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Its only advantage over urn is a larger range; @autoclear refills when empty.
ej.urn.function: Outputs random numbers without repeats until all have been used.

ej.vdb-sig~.builtin_alternative: delay~ (its ramp message smooths delay-time changes)
ej.vdb-sig~.comments: Abstraction; needs a tapin~ connected to its left inlet. Uses two crossfading taps. Argument sets the window size.
ej.vdb-sig~.function: Delays audio with a signal-controlled time and no clicks or pitch shifts.

ej.vdb~.builtin_alternative: delay~ (its ramp message smooths delay-time changes)
ej.vdb~.comments: Abstraction; needs a tapin~ connected to its left inlet. Arguments: window size, delay time. Optimized version of Benjamin Thigpen's vdb~.
ej.vdb~.function: Delays audio with a changeable time and no clicks or pitch shifts.

ej.x2dx.comments: Type it as mxj ej.x2dx. Needs a Java runtime (JDK); none was found on this Mac, so it will not load. Inverse of ej.dx2x.
ej.x2dx.function: Outputs the differences between successive values in a list.

jit.fullscreen.comments: Abstraction for the old matrix-to-window workflow. Its jit. name looks built-in but is not.
jit.fullscreen.function: Opens a jit.window on a second screen and toggles fullscreen with Escape.

jit.getparam.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
jit.getparam.comments: Abstraction; argument is the name of a receive wired into the target object. Its jit. name looks built-in but is not. defaults does not work on every object.
jit.getparam.function: Lists a Jitter object's attributes in a menu and gets or sets them.

kaf.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
kaf.comments: Mac only; needs the third-party shell external, which here comes from the Samplor package as an Intel-only binary, so it will not load in native Apple Silicon Max.
kaf.function: Quits and relaunches the macOS Finder from Max.

kd&u.category: Gesture & hardware: computer keyboard, mouse & game controllers
kd&u.comments: Abstraction. Arguments: key code, modifier number (default 0 on Mac, 128 on Windows).
kd&u.function: Outputs 1 when a chosen key goes down and 0 when it comes up.

ptt.category: Audio I/O: gain, mixers & channel strips
ptt.comments: Abstraction. Hold alt+cmd to talk; ctrl+cmd sets the maximum. Arguments: maximum level, level while talking. Keys are Mac-oriented.
ptt.function: Ducks an audio signal while a modifier-key combination is held (push to talk).

splay~.comments: Abstraction; argument sets channel count. Shortcuts use the numeric keypad. Old interface design.
splay~.function: Plays sound files with a small interface and keyboard shortcuts.

stout~.category: Audio I/O: hardware inputs, outputs & audio settings
stout~.comments: Abstraction. Arguments pick output channels. Shortcuts need the ctrl key since Max 5. Old interface design.
stout~.function: Stereo output stage with faders, meters, input switch and DSP shortcuts.

filter.bessel.comments: Filters a stream of numbers. The docs say it is meant mainly for plotting filter responses; use the ~ version for audio.
filter.bessel.function: Filters a number stream with an Nth-order Bessel filter.

filter.bessel~.function: Filters audio with an Nth-order Bessel filter, which keeps phase smooth.

filter.butterworth.comments: Filters a stream of numbers. The docs say it is meant mainly for plotting filter responses; use the ~ version for audio.
filter.butterworth.function: Filters a number stream with an Nth-order Butterworth filter.

filter.butterworth~.function: Filters audio with an Nth-order Butterworth filter, flat in the passband.

filter.chebyshev1.comments: Filters a stream of numbers. The docs say it is meant mainly for plotting filter responses; use the ~ version for audio.
filter.chebyshev1.function: Filters a number stream with an Nth-order Chebyshev Type I filter.

filter.chebyshev1~.function: Filters audio with a steep Chebyshev Type I filter that ripples in the passband.

filter.chebyshev2.comments: Filters a stream of numbers. The docs say it is meant mainly for plotting filter responses; use the ~ version for audio.
filter.chebyshev2.function: Filters a number stream with an Nth-order Chebyshev Type II filter.

filter.chebyshev2~.function: Filters audio with a Chebyshev Type II filter that ripples in the stopband.

filter.dcblock~.builtin_alternative: biquad~ or svf~ set to a very low highpass
filter.dcblock~.function: Removes DC offset from an audio signal.

filter.elliptic.comments: Filters a stream of numbers. The docs say it is meant mainly for plotting filter responses; use the ~ version for audio.
filter.elliptic.function: Filters a number stream with an Nth-order elliptic filter.

filter.elliptic~.function: Filters audio with an elliptic filter, the steepest rolloff for its order.

filter.jit.bessel.comments: Works on Jitter matrices, such as images, not on audio.
filter.jit.bessel.function: Filters Jitter matrix data with an Nth-order Bessel filter.

filter.jit.butterworth.comments: Works on Jitter matrices, such as images, not on audio.
filter.jit.butterworth.function: Filters Jitter matrix data with an Nth-order Butterworth filter.

filter.jit.chebyshev1.comments: Works on Jitter matrices, such as images, not on audio.
filter.jit.chebyshev1.function: Filters Jitter matrix data with a Chebyshev Type I filter.

filter.jit.chebyshev2.comments: Works on Jitter matrices, such as images, not on audio.
filter.jit.chebyshev2.function: Filters Jitter matrix data with a Chebyshev Type II filter.

filter.jit.elliptic.comments: Works on Jitter matrices, such as images, not on audio.
filter.jit.elliptic.function: Filters Jitter matrix data with an elliptic filter.

filter.jit.legendre.comments: Works on Jitter matrices, such as images, not on audio.
filter.jit.legendre.function: Filters Jitter matrix data with a Legendre filter.

filter.legendre.comments: Filters a stream of numbers. The docs say it is meant mainly for plotting filter responses; use the ~ version for audio.
filter.legendre.function: Filters a number stream with an Nth-order Legendre filter.

filter.legendre~.function: Filters audio with a Legendre filter, steeper than Butterworth without ripple.

filter.one~.function: Filters audio with a basic one-pole lowpass or highpass.

grainflow.chorus~.comments: Built on grainflow.live~. Values between 0 and 1 work best. Accepts grainflow~ messages too.
grainflow.chorus~.function: Granular chorus from one amount value, with random panning.

grainflow.freeze~.comments: Velocity sets loudness; the note's pitch is ignored. Most grainflow~ messages work too.
grainflow.freeze~.function: Freezes and slowly widens a moment of live audio while a MIDI note is held.

grainflow.function2D.comments: Its digest and refpage title are copied from other objects; the help file shows what it really does.
grainflow.function2D.function: XY pad sequencer that glides between points with one or more trackers.

grainflow.harmonize~.category: Audio effects: pitch shift & time stretch
grainflow.harmonize~.comments: Latency follows grain size; supports EDO tunings with notesPerOctave. Accepts grainflow~ messages too.
grainflow.harmonize~.function: Granular harmonizer: MIDI notes add pitch-shifted voices of live input.

grainflow.live~.comments: Args: buffer length and max grains. One output channel per grain, so follow with a panner.
grainflow.live~.function: Granulates live input by recording it into its own buffer.

grainflow.scrubSynth~.function: Noisy granular synth built on frequency and traversal ratios.

grainflow.spat.3dspread.function: Places each new grain at a random point around a 3D center.

grainflow.spat.format.comments: Targets include Spat Gris and the IEM Suite; some go out over OSC with udpsend.
grainflow.spat.format.function: Converts grain positions into messages for other spatializers.

grainflow.spat.pan~.comments: Takes grains as mc channels plus positions from a grainflow.spat.* position object.
grainflow.spat.pan~.function: Pans each grain to a speaker array by distance or vector panning.

grainflow.spat.phys.comments: Extend it through its lambda outlet with the phys.* helpers or your own Jitter code.
grainflow.spat.phys.function: Simple particle physics for grain positions: position, velocity, acceleration.

grainflow.spat.phys.add.comments: Only works in grainflow.spat.phys's lambda loop.
grainflow.spat.phys.add.function: Adds a value to a physics field every frame, inside spat.phys's loop.

grainflow.spat.phys.drag.comments: Only works in grainflow.spat.phys's lambda loop.
grainflow.spat.phys.drag.function: Applies drag to grain movement inside spat.phys's loop.

grainflow.spat.phys.magnets.comments: Magnets are x, y, z, range, strength lists.
grainflow.spat.phys.magnets.function: Pulls or pushes grains around magnet points inside spat.phys's loop.

grainflow.spat.phys.transform.comments: Only works in grainflow.spat.phys's lambda loop.
grainflow.spat.phys.transform.function: Translates, scales or rotates a physics field every frame.

grainflow.spat.speakers.function: Loads speaker layouts from presets, JSON or text files.

grainflow.spat.spirograph.function: Sets each new grain's position by sampling x, y, z signals.

grainflow.spat.split.function: Splits grain position messages by a range of grain IDs.

grainflow.spat.transform.comments: Bang to update all stored points.
grainflow.spat.transform.function: Translates, scales or rotates grain positions, optionally at random.

grainflow.spat.transformOverLife.function: Moves each grain's position over the grain's lifetime.

grainflow.spat.volume.function: Places new grains at random points inside a 3D shape or mesh.

grainflow.spatview~.function: Shows speakers and grain positions for grainflow.spat.pan~.

grainflow.streams~.comments: Adds one signal vector of delay (sends inside poly~).
grainflow.streams~.function: Groups grains into streams you can control separately.

grainflow.sustain~.comments: Overdubs a 250 ms buffer based on input level.
grainflow.sustain~.function: Stereo granular hold effect that smears a short recent buffer.

grainflow.synth~.comments: Notes transpose from MIDI note 60; adsr sets each voice's envelope.
grainflow.synth~.function: Polyphonic granular sampler played with MIDI notes.

grainflow.util.3dspread.comments: Its partner grainflow.util.vbap3d is deprecated; the current spatializers are the grainflow.spat.* objects, such as grainflow.spat.3dspread.
grainflow.util.3dspread.function: Older generator of 3D grain positions for grainflow.util.vbap3d.

grainflow.util.bphasor~.function: Phasor whose speed matches a buffer's length and playback rate.

grainflow.util.grainRecord~.function: Records input into a buffer grain by grain to fake more grains cheaply.

grainflow.util.listChange.builtin_alternative: zl.change — tells only whether the whole list changed
grainflow.util.listChange.category: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
grainflow.util.listChange.function: Reports which list items changed and in which direction.

grainflow.util.list~.comments: Useful for choosing per-grain values from a bank.
grainflow.util.list~.function: Picks values from a list using a 0–1 signal.

grainflow.util.multiPan~.comments: Compiled external; file name is lowercase multipan~.
grainflow.util.multiPan~.function: Equal-power circular panning of grains over any number of speakers.

grainflow.util.phasor~.function: Phasor that wraps or folds between low and high loop points.

grainflow.util.randomRangeList.function: Makes a list of N random numbers between a minimum and maximum.

grainflow.util.rateSizePhasor~.builtin_alternative: mc.snowphasor~ — the help file suggests it as another clock
grainflow.util.rateSizePhasor~.function: Turns grain rate and size into grain-clock phasors for grainflow~.

grainflow.util.record~.builtin_alternative: record~ — help says its record position is too loose for live granulation
grainflow.util.record~.function: Buffer recorder with an accurate record position, overdub and freeze.

grainflow.util.sahRandom~.function: Makes a new random value for each grain when that grain ends.

grainflow.util.stereoPan~.comments: Compiled external; file name is lowercase stereopan~.
grainflow.util.stereoPan~.function: Pans each new grain to a random stereo spot with equal power.

grainflow.waveform~.comments: Can be CPU heavy; lower fps to reduce load.
grainflow.waveform~.function: Waveform display showing grains; also scrubs, selects or loops.

grainflow~.comments: Needs a buffer~ and a grain-clock phasor signal. Grains come out as mc channels, so pan them. The trigger message was removed in 2.0.
grainflow~.function: Multichannel granulator: each grain is its own channel, clocked by a phasor.

gtm.markov.comments: Input: list of up to 128 integers 0–127. Bang the middle inlet for each value. Built with RNBO; wait for the compile-done bang.
gtm.markov.function: Learns a note list and generates new values from a second-order Markov chain.

gtm.markov~.comments: Signal-clocked version of gtm.markov. Same input limit: up to 128 integers 0–127.
gtm.markov~.function: Generates second-order Markov values, stepping each time a phasor~ restarts.

..function: Turns any message into a bang.

180wrap.function: Wraps an angle in degrees into the range −180 to +180.

3Dcartopol.function: Converts 3D x, y, z coordinates into distance, azimuth and elevation.

3Dmatrix.comments: File is 3Dmatrix.mxo. Works on plain number lists, no Jitter needed. The order of operations is settable.
3Dmatrix.function: Translates, scales, rotates and skews 3D points in a chosen order.

3Dpoltocar.comments: Uses a left-handed coordinate system. Argument sets the mode.
3Dpoltocar.function: Converts distance, azimuth and elevation into 3D x, y, z coordinates.

_.comments: Typed as _ (file underscore.mxo). The prefix is changed with a set message.
_.function: Puts a word, set by default, in front of any message.

__.comments: Typed as __ (file underscoremulti.mxo). One inlet per argument.
__.function: Puts a different prefix in front of messages at each inlet.

a2db~.comments: Float output works with audio off.
a2db~.function: Converts linear amplitude to decibels for signals or numbers.

bartime.comments: Arguments: time signature, time units per beat, beat division.
bartime.function: Converts a running time count into bars, beats and ticks.

bcf2000.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
bcf2000.comments: Arguments set the resolution of two controller ranges.
bcf2000.function: Parses high-resolution NRPN controller data, as sent by a Behringer BCF2000.

bezier.comments: Works on number lists, so it can drive any parameter. Argument 0 = 2D, 1 = 3D.
bezier.function: Computes points along a 2D or 3D Bézier curve from control points.

bitlist.comments: Supports set bit widths, signed or unsigned, and zero padding. Lists above 52 bits act oddly.
bitlist.function: Converts an integer to a list of bits and back.

bits2int.comments: bitlist does the same with more options.
bits2int.function: Converts a list of 32 bits into an integer.

bspline.function: Computes a point along a B-spline curve through control points.

bytecount.comments: Outputs −1 if the file is not found. Accepts search-path names or absolute paths.
bytecount.function: Reports the size of a file in bytes.

ccext.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
ccext.comments: Modes also filter repeats and jitter (replaces Eric Singer's deflutter).
ccext.function: Merges two 7-bit MIDI controller values into one 14-bit value.

ceil.function: Rounds a float up to the next integer.

centlist.comments: Outputs the position and the interpolated value there.
centlist.function: Finds the center of gravity of a list of values.

changelist.category: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
changelist.comments: Handles numbers, symbols and mixed lists. Can lock the comparison value.
changelist.function: Passes a list only when it differs from the previous one.

checklist.category: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
checklist.comments: Mode 1 reports only when the match state changes.
checklist.function: Compares incoming data with a stored item and reports a match.

compare.comments: Outputs 0, 1 or 2, and −1 for a number-versus-symbol mismatch.
compare.function: Reports whether one item is smaller, equal or larger than another.

comport.comments: From IEM (Winfried Ritsch). The help warns it can open any file on the system.
comport.function: Opens and talks to a serial port, ported from Pure Data.

copysign.function: Gives a value the sign of a second value.

createfolder.comments: On Windows it cannot create nested folders and errors if the folder exists.
createfolder.function: Creates a folder on disk, including missing parent folders.

d2r.function: Converts degrees to radians, with optional offset and wrapping.

datatype.function: Reports whether input is an int, float, symbol, list or other message.

db*~.category: Audio I/O: gain, mixers & channel strips
db*~.comments: File is dbmult~.mxo. Numbers from 0 up are read as MIDI fader values; negative numbers as dB.
db*~.function: Multiplies a signal by a gain in dB, with smooth changes.

db2a~.comments: Integers are read as MIDI values mapped from +12 to −96 dB. Arguments: MIDI value for 0 dB (default 84), ramp time for line~.
db2a~.function: Converts decibels to linear amplitude for signals or numbers, with MIDI input mode.

dcblocker~.comments: coef message sets the cutoff (default about 10 Hz).
dcblocker~.function: Removes DC offset from a signal with a one-pole, one-zero filter.

deltalist.comments: The right list sets the output length.
deltalist.function: Subtracts one list from another element by element.

detox.comments: Reads one line at a time; pairs with toxine and intox. Max has no built-in XML parser.
detox.function: Pulls tag names, attributes and content out of XML lines.

dist~.comments: Argument is the dB drop per distance unit. Outputs a signal gain.
dist~.function: Turns a distance into a gain that drops by set dB per unit.

duplist.category: Lists & data: sorting, shuffling & set operations
duplist.function: Removes duplicate numbers from a list.

dynroute.comments: Can pass the first element through. Based on jhno's xroute.
crossref: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
dynroute.function: Routes messages by a selector and position that can change live.

euler_constant.function: Outputs e, or a number multiplied by e or 1/e.

exp.function: Raises e to the power of the input.

exp2.function: Raises 2 to the power of the input.

filemanager.comments: Mac only. Delete cannot be undone. Also reports system paths into a dict.
filemanager.function: Copies, moves, renames, deletes and lists files and folders.

floor.function: Rounds a float down to the next integer.

fromascii.category: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
fromascii.function: Converts ASCII character codes into symbols and numbers.

gaze.comments: Gives 2D screen positions without OpenGL rendering.
gaze.function: Projects 3D points onto a 2D view with camera and field-of-view settings.

getenv.comments: On Mac this loads a patcher that uses shell commands; on Windows it is an external.
getenv.function: Reads a system environment variable such as a home folder.

getpaths.function: Outputs common system folder paths such as desktop and user library.

goldensection.function: Multiplies a number by the golden ratio and its reciprocal.

groupid.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
groupid.comments: Reuses freed numbers. Useful for instance numbers in duplicated abstractions.
groupid.function: Hands out unique ID numbers to object copies within a group.

heading.comments: Arguments: scale factor and x/y offset.
heading.function: Converts joystick x/y tilt into heading angle and total tilt.

hexlist.category: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
hexlist.comments: Made for a serial display protocol.
hexlist.function: Converts eight ASCII hex digits into an integer.

hsv2rgb.comments: All values 0–1. Argument 1 converts RGB back to HSV.
hsv2rgb.function: Converts colors between HSV and RGB.

hypot.comments: Gives the distance of a point from the center.
hypot.function: Computes the hypotenuse from two sides.

idx.comments: Settable min, max, step and lock at the top of the range.
idx.function: Counts inputs and puts an index number in front of each message.

insertlist.category: Lists & data: get, insert & remove items
insertlist.function: Inserts items into a stored list at a position.

interpol.comments: Values beyond 0–1 extrapolate. Do not mix @ attributes with plain arguments.
interpol.function: Interpolates between two lists by a 0–1 position or in steps.

intox.function: Indents XML lines for writing formatted files.

ldexp.function: Multiplies a value by 2 to a given power.

logb.function: Outputs the binary exponent of a number.

mathlist.comments: Operation is the first argument, e.g. mathlist >> 8.
mathlist.function: Applies one math or bit operation to every element of a list.

memchr.comments: C string function. Mode swaps which input is searched.
memchr.function: Finds the position of a character within the first n characters of a symbol.

memcmp.function: Compares the first n characters of two symbols.

memcpy.function: Copies n characters from one symbol into another.

memmove.function: Copies n characters between symbols at set positions.

memset.function: Overwrites n characters of a symbol with one character.

mmmlist.comments: Can also work on a running stream of values.
mmmlist.function: Outputs the minimum, maximum and mean of a list.

mtx.comments: Groups work across all open patches. Group can be set by argument, attribute or message.
mtx.function: Makes copies in a named group act as mutually exclusive on/off switches.

multisplit.comments: Outputs the range index, or −1 out of range. Split points can change live.
multisplit.function: Sorts numbers into ranges set by split points.

n!.function: Computes the factorial of an integer.

nn2bits.comments: bitlist does the same with more options.
nn2bits.function: Converts an integer into a list of 32 bits.

p4mat.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
p4mat.function: Formats messages for sending to pattrforward.

panner~.comments: Abstraction. Argument sets the start position.
panner~.function: Pans a mono signal between two outputs with constant power.

peakfollow~.comments: Argument is the decay time in ms (default 1000). Second outlet shows rising or falling.
peakfollow~.function: Follows signal peaks instantly and lets them decay exponentially.

peaklist.comments: Also reports the zero-based index. If the top value appears twice, the later one wins.
peaklist.function: Finds the highest value in a list and its position.

pi_constant.function: Outputs pi, or a number multiplied by pi or 1/pi.

piwrap.function: Wraps an angle in radians into the range −pi to +pi.

pop.comments: Positive count repeats; negative count filters.
pop.function: Repeats a bang several times, or passes only every nth bang.

posit.category: Patching utilities: scripting, presets & patcher control
posit.comments: Can also query, move and rename named objects, and list all coll and buffer~ names.
posit.function: Reports class, scripting name and position of objects in open patches.

processes.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
processes.comments: Mac only and experimental. The help warns some functions crash Max.
processes.function: Sends show, hide, activate or kill commands to other running apps.

r2d.function: Converts radians to degrees, with optional offset and wrapping.

replacelist.category: Lists & data: get, insert & remove items
replacelist.function: Replaces items in a stored list at a position.

rgb2yuv.comments: Offset for YUV black level is settable (default 16).
rgb2yuv.function: Converts color values between RGB and YUV.

rotatexyz.comments: Output can drive a rotate message for OpenGL objects.
rotatexyz.function: Converts x, y, z rotation angles into an angle-axis rotation.

slicelist.category: Lists & data: get, insert & remove items
slicelist.comments: Arguments: number of outlets and slice size. Also has a single-slice mode.
slicelist.function: Cuts a list into equal sublists sent to separate outlets.

slidelist.comments: Works element by element on whole lists.
slidelist.function: Smooths lists, ints and floats with a slide filter.

statlist.comments: One object for many list statistics.
statlist.function: Computes mean, deviations, variance, skew, kurtosis, min and max of a list.

str2ul.function: Converts the letters of a symbol to upper or lower case.

strcat.comments: C string function. Mode swaps the order.

strchr.function: Finds the first position of a character in a symbol.

strcmp.function: Reports whether two symbols are equal or which sorts first.

strcoll.function: Compares two symbols using the system's language sort order.

strcpy.comments: The help itself calls it somewhat useless in Max.

strcspn.function: Counts characters before the first match from a character set.

strcut.comments: Pairs with strrchr to split file paths.
strcut.function: Cuts a symbol at a position into two parts.

streamlist.comments: Up to 1024 items. Big lists can crash older objects with small list limits.
streamlist.function: Keeps a rolling list of the most recent values.

strfilt.comments: Up to 12 character-type filters at once.
strfilt.function: Keeps only characters of chosen types, such as digits or letters.

stricmp.function: Compares two symbols ignoring upper and lower case.

strlen.function: Reports the number of characters in a symbol.

strncat.function: Appends the first n characters of one symbol to another.

strncmp.function: Compares the first n characters of two symbols.

strncpy.function: Copies the first n characters of one symbol into another.

strpbrk.comments: Handy for pulling numbers out of file names.
strpbrk.function: Finds the first character from a set, such as digits in a name.

strrchr.comments: Pairs with strcut to split file paths.
strrchr.function: Finds the last position of a character in a symbol.

strrcut.function: Removes the part of a symbol before a position.

strspn.function: Counts leading characters that belong to a character set.

strstr.comments: C string function. Its help file demonstrates strspn instead, so port counts are unconfirmed. Port counts unconfirmed: no saved example box.
strstr.function: Finds the position of one symbol inside another.

strtok.function: Splits a symbol into pieces at a delimiter.

sumlist.function: Adds up all numbers in a list.

timestamp.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
timestamp.function: Outputs the system date, time and milliseconds.

timex.comments: Accepts many shorthand time formats. Floats get rounding errors above about 18 hours.
timex.function: Converts between milliseconds and hours:minutes:seconds:ms text.

toascii.category: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
toascii.function: Converts symbols and numbers into ASCII character codes.

toxine.comments: Pairs with detox and intox for XML files.
toxine.function: Reads and writes text files one line at a time.

xframe~.comments: Feed it from fft~. Based on frame~ by j.jester.
xframe~.function: Turns FFT frames into a list of bin amplitudes plus spectrum statistics.

xorlist.category: Lists & data: bytes, encodings & buffer conversion
xorlist.function: Computes a running XOR checksum over a list of integers.

jk.lpx.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
jk.lpx.comments: Use one per pad; @pad or @button picks it, @mode sets toggle, button or radio. Use with jk.lpxcore, as in the help patch. Novation Launchpad X only.
jk.lpx.function: Links one Launchpad X pad or button to a live.text or live.menu.

jk.lpxcore.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
jk.lpxcore.comments: Use one per patch alongside jk.lpx objects. Novation Launchpad X only.
jk.lpxcore.function: Sets up Launchpad X MIDI ports, colors and a random light show.

karma~.builtin_alternative: groove~ with record~ (more wiring for live looping)
karma~.comments: Needs a buffer~ name argument; second argument sets 1, 2 or 4 channels. Messages: record, play, stop, append, overdub. The inlet after the audio inputs sets speed.
karma~.function: Records, loops and overdubs into a buffer~ with variable speed.

mat.oocall.builtin_alternative: send / receive — one-way broadcast with no reply; value, coll or dict already reply to the box that asks.
mat.oocall.category: Patching utilities: abstraction arguments & shared code
mat.oocall.comments: Methods must reply at once: no delay or defer. A numeric @parent is silently dropped. Help files spell it mat.ooCall; the file name is lowercase.
mat.oocall.function: Calls shared patch code by name and outputs its reply.

mat.oomethod.builtin_alternative: send / receive — one-way broadcast with no reply.
mat.oomethod.category: Patching utilities: abstraction arguments & shared code
mat.oomethod.comments: Method names are global: two methods with one name both reply. Use #1.name inside abstractions for per-instance methods.
mat.oomethod.function: Holds shared patch code that mat.oocall boxes call by name.

jit.ml.lzw.comments: Mainly for estimating how complex or novel data is.
jit.ml.lzw.function: Compresses or decompresses Jitter matrices with LZW coding.

ml.art.comments: Unsupervised and online: no training phase. @vigilance sets how fine the categories are.
ml.art.function: Sorts inputs into categories it creates itself while learning.

ml.fcm.function: Clusters lists so each point can partly belong to several clusters.

ml.hmm.comments: Intel-only on Mac (x86_64 binary, confirmed in release notes), so it will not load in native Apple Silicon Max.
ml.hmm.function: Learns and predicts sequences with a hidden Markov model.

ml.kdtree.comments: fluid.kdtree~ is the better-maintained choice if FluCoMa is installed.
ml.kdtree.function: Stores lists and finds the nearest ones quickly.

ml.lzw.function: Compresses symbol or number sequences, for measuring their complexity.

ml.markov.comments: Supports higher orders with @order. Package licence asks commercial users to contact the author.
ml.markov.function: Learns event sequences and generates new ones with a Markov chain.

ml.mlp.comments: Older and simpler than fluid.mlpregressor~ and fluid.mlpclassifier~.
ml.mlp.function: Learns input-to-output mappings with a small neural network.

ml.principle.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
ml.principle.comments: Send example lists, then bang or calc to analyze.
ml.principle.function: Learns principal components from example lists, then projects new lists.

ml.scale.comments: Learns the distribution from incoming data; @inverse undoes the scaling.
crossref: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
ml.scale.function: Scales lists to zero mean and unit standard deviation.

ml.som.category: Machine learning: data sets, scaling & dimension reduction
ml.som.comments: Package example patches use it for grain, MIDI and spectral maps.
ml.som.function: Maps lists onto a 2D grid where similar inputs land close together.

ml.spatial.function: Encodes recent integer tokens as a decaying memory vector.

ml.vmm.bin.comments: Its refpage says accuracy is very poor compared with the other ml.vmm objects.
ml.vmm.bin.function: Predicts sequences with a binary context-tree variable-order Markov model.

ml.vmm.dct.function: Learns symbol or number sequences and predicts or generates continuations with a decomposed context-tree model.

ml.vmm.lzms.function: Predicts sequences with a Lempel-Ziv variable-order Markov model.

ml.vmm.ppm.function: Predicts sequences with prediction-by-partial-match, learning as data arrives.

ml.vmm.pst.function: Predicts sequences with a probabilistic suffix tree Markov model.

mo.adc~.builtin_alternative: mc.adc~ — no gain stage built in
mo.adc~.category: Audio I/O: hardware inputs, outputs & audio settings
mo.adc~.comments: Restart DSP after the channel count changes (modulo README).
mo.adc~.function: Takes multichannel audio input with a gain slider per channel.

mo.arrow.builtin_alternative: key — outputs raw key codes; filter them yourself
mo.arrow.category: Gesture & hardware: computer keyboard, mouse & game controllers
mo.arrow.function: Triggers events from the computer keyboard's arrow keys.

mo.average.builtin_alternative: mean — averages a stream of single numbers over time
mo.average.function: Outputs the average of a list, with absolute mode and sensitivity.

mo.calibrate.comments: Start the window, move the sensor through its full range, and the module stores the extremes (use_when).
mo.calibrate.function: Learns the minimum and maximum of incoming data over a time window.

mo.click.function: Turns clicks or key presses into single, double and hold events.

mo.cpu.builtin_alternative: adstatus — reports CPU load, no display
mo.cpu.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
mo.cpu.function: Shows Max's CPU load at a chosen polling rate.

mo.crosspatch.builtin_alternative: crosspatch with matrix — same editor, no modulo list handling
mo.crosspatch.category: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
mo.crosspatch.comments: Click a cable and press Backspace to delete it.
mo.crosspatch.function: Routes list elements from inputs to outputs by drawing cables.

mo.crosspatch~.comments: Restart DSP after the channel count changes (modulo README).
mo.crosspatch~.function: Routes multichannel audio between inputs and outputs by drawing cables.

mo.ctlout.function: Sends MIDI control changes to a device picked from a menu.

mo.ctlouts.function: Sends a list of values as several MIDI control changes.

mo.cue.builtin_alternative: counter — counts, but stores no cue data
mo.cue.function: Stores numbered cues and steps through them to trigger events.

mo.dac~.builtin_alternative: mc.dac~ — no gain stage built in
mo.dac~.category: Audio I/O: hardware inputs, outputs & audio settings
mo.dac~.comments: Restart DSP after the channel count changes (modulo README).
mo.dac~.function: Sends multichannel audio to the hardware with a gain slider per channel.

mo.date.category: Patching utilities: Max app, system & date
mo.date.function: Shows and outputs today's date and time.

mo.debounce.builtin_alternative: speedlim — limits rate but sends the last value later
mo.debounce.comments: Try about 500 ms for mechanical buttons (use_when).
crossref: Rhythm & time: delays, gates & bang logic
mo.debounce.function: Ignores repeat triggers that arrive too soon, cleaning up jittery buttons.

mo.dial.function: Row of dials, one per list value, ready for MIDI mapping.

mo.encoder.category: Gesture & hardware: MIDI, grid & touch controllers
mo.encoder.function: Dial driven by a relative MIDI encoder (63/65 style steps).

mo.fm~.comments: Help lists carrier, harmonicity, ratio and rate as the list order.
mo.fm~.function: Simple FM synth voice played by a 0–1 list or messages.

mo.gain~.category: Audio I/O: gain, mixers & channel strips
mo.gain~.function: Multichannel gain slider; Shift-drag moves every channel.

mo.ggate.builtin_alternative: gate — outlet chosen by an integer
mo.ggate.category: Lists & data: change detection, matching & routing
mo.ggate.comments: The control range is divided equally between the outlets.
mo.ggate.function: Sends input out one of several outlets, chosen by one value.

mo.granulator~.comments: Load a sample or folder by drag and drop; control it with a 0–1 list or named messages.
mo.granulator~.function: Eight-phase stereo granular sampler with its own panel.

mo.grid.builtin_alternative: live.grid — the grid UI without a clock
mo.grid.function: Grid step sequencer with step count, constraints and play direction.

mo.gridmeter~.comments: Click a cell to mute or unmute that channel.
mo.gridmeter~.function: Shows many audio channels' levels as a grid of lit cells.

mo.hi.category: Gesture & hardware: computer keyboard, mouse & game controllers
mo.hi.function: Reads trackpads, gamepads and other HID devices picked from a menu.

mo.hrslider.function: Horizontal range sliders, each setting a low and high value.

mo.htab.category: UI: buttons, pads, tabs & color pickers
mo.htab.function: Horizontal tabs with named items for picking a state.

mo.if.function: Compares input to a value with a condition picked from a menu.

mo.joystick.category: Gesture & hardware: computer keyboard, mouse & game controllers
mo.joystick.function: Fires events when joystick axes pass high or low thresholds.

mo.key.category: Gesture & hardware: computer keyboard, mouse & game controllers
mo.key.function: Triggers events from the space, escape or return keys.

mo.keyboard.function: On-screen keyboard that outputs notes and can send MIDI.

mo.latch.function: Outputs the greater or lower value from a list, by mode.

mo.launch.comments: Drag and drop the target in, then bang to launch.

mo.led.category: UI: buttons, pads, tabs & color pickers
mo.led.function: Row of LED indicators, one per list value.

mo.makenote.function: Makes MIDI notes with pitch, velocity, duration and a play probability.

mo.map.builtin_alternative: mappings — Max's own MIDI and key mapping

mo.matrix~.function: Grid of clickable cells routing multichannel audio.
